papers.title: Utilizing silica-enriched filter cake as a cement replacement and rheology modifier in 3D-printable mortar containing coffee husk and palm leaf ashes
papers.journal: Multiscale and Multidisciplinary Modeling Experiments and Design
papers.abstract: Abstract This study evaluates a novel combination of coffee husk ash (CHA), palm leaf ash (PLA), and silica-enriched filter cake (SEFC) for extrusion-based 3D concrete printing (3DCP), where CHA and PLA serve as waste-derived supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) and SEFC functions both SCM and as a rheology-modifying additive to enhance fresh and hardened performance. Physicochemical characterization revealed high silica contents in SEFC (80.6%), CHA (39.3%), and PLA (42.4%), with elevated specific surface areas compared to ordinary Portland cement (OPC), indicating potential pozzolanic characteristics. X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed the presence of amorphous phases favorable for hydration reactions. SEFC significantly improved rheological behavior, enhancing extrudability, shape retention, and buildability, enabling stable layer-by-layer printing. Fresh-state results indicated controlled workability loss and suitable setting behavior for layer-by-layer deposition. In the hardened state, SEFC-modified mortar (optimized mix) exhibited compressive strength improvements of 19.3% and 12.8% at 7 and 28 days, respectively, compared to the CHA–PLA reference mixture (M11). Microstructural analysis showed a denser matrix with reduced porosity and increased calcium silicate hydrate formation, explaining the improved mechanical performance. Overall, CHA, PLA, and SEFC demonstrate strong potential as SCMs and functional additives for 3DCP, contributing to reduced cement consumption and circular waste valorization.

papers.title: Pharmaceutical Crystalline Complex of Methylparaben with Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API): Preparation, Structural Characterization, and Solid-State Properties
authors: Santhosh Kumar M Praveen Kumar G
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, two novel drug–drug (1 : 1) crystalline complexes of methylparaben (MP) with amantadine (AMA) and rotigotine (ROT) were synthesized and systematically investigated. The crystalline complexes were prepared using the slow solvent evaporation technique, using the free-base forms of the APIs prepared from their hydrochloride salts. Formation of the new solid phases was confirmed through comprehensive solid-state characterization using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, UV-visible spectroscopy, Differential Scanning Calorimetry, Powder X-ray Diffraction, Single-Crystal X-ray Diffraction, and 1H NMR spectroscopy. Distinct changes in spectral features, diffraction patterns, and thermal behaviour established the successful generation of crystalline complexes different from the parent drug components. The study highlights the effectiveness of drug–drug co-crystallization involving amine-containing CNS drugs as a viable strategy for modulating the solid-state properties of pharmaceutical ingredients.

papers.title: Matrix-derived hypoallergenicity: potential roles of Beta vulgaris polyphenols and betalamic acid in PR-10 allergen modulation
papers.abstract: Cold-pressed apple, carrot, and celery juices retain native PR-10 allergens associated with Pollen-Food Allergy Syndrome, whereas thermal processing can alter allergen recognition while compromising heat-sensitive nutrients and sensory quality. We propose matrix-derived hypoallergenicity, a framework in which food-matrix chemistry may regulate allergen accessibility. Using beetroot ( Beta vulgaris ) as a model matrix, we examine two chemically plausible pathways, polyphenol-derived quinone modification and betalamic-acid-mediated carbonyl chemistry. Neither pathway has been validated in authentic juice systems. This perspective, therefore, defines a testable framework for modulating allergen behavior while preserving nutritional and sensory quality.

papers.title: Multi-scale convolution with efficient channel attention improves benign–malignant classification of spinal tumors on T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI
papers.abstract: Background Accurate differentiation between benign and malignant spinal tumors is critical for treatment planning, yet manual interpretation of T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI remains subjective, with substantial inter-observer variability. This study aimed to develop a deep learning model, the multi-scale deep residual network (MSDR-Net), for automated benign–malignant classification. Methods A total of 500 T2-weighted fat-suppressed MR images of pathologically confirmed spinal tumors (389 benign, 111 malignant) were retrospectively collected from two institutions. Data were partitioned into training (70%), validation (20%), and independent test (10%) sets, and five-fold cross-validation was performed. Leave-one-center-out external validation was also performed (development: Institution A, n = 300; evaluation: Institution B, n = 200). The proposed MSDR-Net incorporates multi-branch residual blocks that combine parallel multi-scale convolutional paths with efficient channel attention modules and was benchmarked against six established architectures. Results On the independent test set (N = 50; 12 malignant cases), MSDR-Net achieved 92.0% accuracy, 91.7% sensitivity (95% CI 61.5%–99.8%), 92.1% specificity, and an AUC of 0.921, the highest point estimates among evaluated architectures. The model was well calibrated (Brier score 0.072), with net benefit over treat-all strategies across thresholds of 0.10–0.60. Derived from a small test cohort, these estimates carry substantial uncertainty and await confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts. External-cohort accuracy was 86.5% (AUC 0.875). Ablation experiments showed that removing either component degraded performance, with a modest super-additive interaction; given their substantially smaller capacity, the single-path variants’ deficit cannot be attributed solely to removing multi-scale processing. The model has 55.4M parameters and 12.3-ms inference per image. Conclusion MSDR-Net effectively captures multi-scale discriminative features of spinal tumors on T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI, achieving high classification accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. The model shows promise for clinical deployment as an auxiliary diagnostic tool for orthopedic surgeons and radiologists.

papers.title: An explainable machine learning pipeline using XGBoost and SHAP to identify factors associated with tuberculosis treatment adherence in a district health center
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) treatment adherence is critical for preventing disease relapse and the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains. Understanding factors associated with non-adherent behavioral profiles can guide targeted counseling interventions, particularly in resource-constrained public health settings. We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional study utilizing survey data from 379 TB outpatients at a district-level medical center. Following the 80/20 split, mode imputation parameters and Boruta feature selection were derived exclusively from the training partition, with training-derived mode values subsequently applied to missing observations in the hold-out test set. SMOTE was applied exclusively to the training data. The performance of an eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier was compared against a SMOTE-balanced Logistic Regression baseline on the independent hold-out test set. The proposed XGBoost + SMOTE model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.768 (95% CI: 0.623-−0.896), a Sensitivity of 47.1% (95% CI: 23.1-−73.3%), and a Specificity of 89.8% (95% CI: 82.0-−96.7%). McNemar’s test ( $$p = 0.4545$$ ) indicated no statistically significant difference in classification performance compared to the SMOTE-balanced Logistic Regression. However, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis provided deeper interpretable insights, revealing that patients’ comprehension of periodic testing schedules and core treatment principles were most strongly associated with adherence behaviors. By identifying non-linear interactions between sociodemographic factors and specific knowledge deficits, the explainable AI framework maps associative risk profiles. This empowers healthcare workers to precisely target educational gaps and prioritize behavioral interventions, serving as a foundation for future longitudinal predictive systems.

papers.title: Hybrid Adaptive Threshold-Based Wearable System for Patient Vital Sign Monitoring and Motion Artifact Mitigation
papers.abstract: Motion artifact from patient movement remains a critical barrier to reliable wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) monitoring in nursing practice, causing false physiological readings and alarm fatigue that compromise patient safety in remote and ambulatory care settings. This study aimed to develop and validate a wearable edge computing system integrating a Hybrid Adaptive Threshold algorithm for personalized motion artifact mitigation and a partial National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS-2) module for automated nursing early warning across heterogeneous patient motion profiles. An experimental quantitative study was conducted on five healthy participants exposed to seven predefined motion scenarios (L0–L6). The prototype integrated a MAX30102 PPG sensor at the finger and an MPU-6050 IMU with an ESP32 microcontroller at the wrist. Performance was evaluated across four dimensions: static vital sign accuracy (MAPE against a commercial pulse oximeter), adaptive calibration under normal and tremor-simulated conditions, Data Gating effectiveness comparing Phase 1 (unfiltered) versus Phase 2 (filter active), and NEWS-2 scoring with MQTT transmission integrity. Static accuracy yielded a mean heart rate MAPE of 0.71% and SpO₂ MAPE of 0.31%. The Hybrid Adaptive Threshold algorithm successfully generated personalized gating boundaries for all participants, including tremor-simulated subjects. Data Gating reduced heart rate output standard deviation by 99.4% during aggressive arm swinging and 92.6% during finger tapping. NEWS-2 scoring executed with zero logical error across all six injection test cases, and MQTT payload integrity reached 100%. The proposed system demonstrated clinically acceptable accuracy, effective personalized motion gating, and reliable automated early warning capability, confirming its potential as a wearable nursing surveillance tool for ambulatory patient populations with heterogeneous motion profiles. Keywords : Photoplethysmography, Motion Artifact, Adaptive Threshold, Edge Computing, Wearable Sensor, NEWS-2.

papers.title: Intermediate‐Phase Blocking as a Kinetic Lever for High Ionic Conductivity of Wet‐Synthesized Cl‐Rich Li Argyrodite for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high ionic conductivity of wet‐synthesized sulfide solid electrolytes remains a critical challenge for enabling scalable all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs). In Cl‐rich Li‐argyrodites, Li + transport is strongly governed by the Cl occupancy at the 4d Wyckoff site, yet conventional wet syntheses fail to control this local structure due to the spontaneous formation of unfavorable intermediate phases. Here, we uncover that the formation of the PS 3 Cl 2− moiety during intermediate heat‐treatment stages suppresses 4d‐site Cl incorporation, thereby limiting ionic conductivity. By introducing controlled amounts of S 8 as a reaction‐kinetic modulator, we show that S–S‐containing precursor environments kinetically hinder PS 3 Cl 2− formation during heat treatment. Multimodal structural analyses (solid‐state NMR, XRD Rietveld refinement, DSC) confirm that increasing S 8 systematically increases 4d‐site Cl occupancy while suppressing the undesired intermediate. This kinetic steering enables the Li 5.5 PS 4.5 Cl 1.5 (LPSCl 1.5 ) electrolyte to reach a high ionic conductivity of 6.06 ± 0.29 mS cm −1 at 25°C without additional specialized processing such as rapid thermal annealing or spark plasma sintering. ASSB half‐cells incorporating this electrolyte exhibit excellent rate capability and 77.8% capacity retention over 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a mechanistic framework for intermediate‐phase engineering in wet synthesis and presents a high‐performance wet‐synthesis route with potential for scale‐up.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of the Explosion Parameters of Selected Gluten-Free Flour Dusts
papers.abstract: Flour dust explosions are chemical explosions characterized by violent thermal decomposition and oxidation reactions, accompanied by a sudden increase in pressure and temperature. Combustible dusts undergo thermal decomposition, releasing flammable gases; thus, in this context, a dust explosion is similar to an explosion of a flammable gas–air mixture. Flour explosions in the food industry have been the subject of many studies, but there is limited number of publications on the explosion safety of gluten-free flours. Five dusts were selected for comparative characterization under common standardized conditions: green pea flour, soybean flour, millet flour, lentil flour, and maize flour. The following parameters were determined: the minimum ignition temperature, the maximum explosion pressure (pmax) and its derivative (dp/dt)max, and the lower explosion limit; Thermogravimetric Analysis; and heat of combustion tests. The tested flours show different values of basic flammability and explosiveness parameters, e.g., the green pea flour 5 mm dust layer ignited from the heated surface at temperatures as low as 310 °C. The lowest temperature of maximum mass loss (291 °C) was recorded for green pea flour. The obtained KSt values range from 55 to 81 bar·m·s−1 (class St 1), the LEL is between 125 and 250 g·m−3, and the 5 mm dust layer MIT values range from 310 to over 400 °C. The results show that there is a need to apply dedicated explosion protection means in plants where the processing, and transportation of the gluten-free flours takes place.

papers.journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
papers.abstract: Chemically amplified resist performance is governed by the combined effects of polymer structure, molecular characteristics, thermal behavior, and processing conditions. In this study, methacrylate-based photoresist polymers were prepared under different chain-transfer-agent (CTA)-mediated polymerization conditions using a multifunctional three-arm RAFT agent, TMP-CEPA3, while maintaining the same nominal HEMA:TCDMA:MAMA feed composition. Line-pattern evaluation over nominal feature sizes of 10–80 μm likewise showed favorable pattern formation for CTA 0 and CTA 8. Overall, increasing TMP-CEPA3 loading did not systematically improve patterning behavior, indicating that resist behavior is governed by the combined effects of polymerization conditions, polymer characteristics, and lithographic processing parameters.

papers.title: Processing‐Driven Engineering of Transparent Conductive In‐Zn‐O Thin Films: A Comparative Study of Spin‐Coating, Inkjet Printing, and Screen Printing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Transparent conductive oxides are essential materials for optoelectronic applications. However, achieving both high electrical conductivity and optical transparency with solution‐compatible deposition techniques remains challenging. In this work, In–Zn–O thin films are fabricated using three complementary solution‐based methods, spin coating, inkjet printing, and screen printing, with tailored solutions optimized for each technique. Although identical thermal treatments are applied, the deposition technique significantly affects film thickness, microstructure, and the resulting optical and electrical properties. All films are amorphous, with grain sizes ranging from a few nanometres to approximately 300 nm, depending on nucleation density controlled by solution concentration. After annealing in a reducing atmosphere, the films exhibit low electrical resistivity (1–100 mΩ cm), high optical transparency (>90% in the visible–NIR range), and direct bandgaps of 3.3–3.6 eV. Spectroscopic ellipsometry indicates uniform optical properties for printed films, while spin‐coated films show slight inhomogeneity linked to their layered microstructure. These results clarify the interplay between solution chemistry, deposition method, and drying conditions in tuning the optoelectronic performance of In–Zn–O thin films. This study presents the first demonstration of conductive and transparent In–Zn–O thin films produced by screen printing.

papers.title: Elevated near-surface Ångström exponent peaks from dualwavelength CLADS over the North China Plain
papers.abstract: Abstract Near-surface aerosol Ångström exponent (AE) profiles are needed for size-related air-quality assessment and to reduce uncertainties in multi-wavelength optical retrievals, yet pulsed lidars typically cannot resolve the lowest few hundred metres and surface in-situ optics lack vertical coverage. Using dual-wavelength (405/532 nm) charge-coupled device–laser aerosol detection system (CLADS)—an imaging lidar with dual laser and dual CCD—we retrieve continuous nocturnal AE and extinction profiles from the ground through the boundary layer over seven nights in November 2018 at Gucheng (North China Plain) during the McFAN campaign. On each of the seven nights, multi-layer AE structure is resolved below ~1.5 km. The central result is a recurrent elevated AE peak: while dual-wavelength extinction is highest at the surface, AE systematically maximizes in the ~110–230 m band (composite median near ~180 m), with a surface-to-peak contrast of ~1.1–1.4 relative to the 10–50 m layer (~1.0–1.3 if the two lowest bins, 10 and 20 m, are excluded and the surface reference is taken as 30–50 m). Aerosol loading and size-sensitive spectral slope are therefore vertically decoupled. Near-surface CLADS extinction at 405 and 532 nm covaries strongly with co-located dry nephelometry (pooled R ≈ 0.88–0.92). By resolving the lower-boundary-layer blind zone, dual-wavelength CLADS indicates that, in these cases, surface-based AE measurements can under-represent the fine-particle-dominated layer aloft, which is relevant to satellite/lidar retrieval constraints and boundary-layer radiative calculations. Nocturnal stable stratification is a plausible but untested explanation, because no concurrent thermodynamic profiles were available.

papers.title: Host seasonal trophic strategies linked to dietary‐microbiota coupling: A potential mechanism mediating the coexistence of sympatric small rodents
papers.abstract: The coexistence mechanisms of sympatric species have long attracted widespread research attention. However, it remains unclear whether sympatric species experiencing the same seasonal conditions exhibit convergent or host-specific gut microbiota responses. We compared the herbivorous Brandt's vole (Lasiopodomys brandtii) and the granivorous Mongolian gerbil (Meriones unguiculatus), two sympatric rodent species with divergent trophic strategies inhabiting the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, China. By integrating plant DNA metabarcoding, gut microbiota profiling and microbial functional output analyses across seasons, we investigated seasonal dietary-microbiome associations. Our results revealed that although seasonal dietary variation affects the composition of the host gut microbiota, the taxonomic and functional plasticity of gut microbiota is strongly influenced by host trophic strategies. Brandt's voles maintained a fermentation-oriented microbiota tightly coupled with seasonal shifts in Poaceae and Cyperaceae intake, exhibiting coordinated changes in microbial taxa, short-chain fatty acid production and cellulase activity. In contrast, Mongolian gerbils exhibited substantial seasonal dietary turnover between Chenopodiaceae and Caragana plants, while maintaining comparatively stable microbial functional outputs, suggesting metabolic buffering. Host trophic strategy, rather than shared environmental seasonality, is related to the strength and functional consequences of the coupling between diet and microbiome. Our results emphasize the gut microbiome as a potential key mechanism underlying trophic niche differentiation and ecological coexistence in wild mammalian communities.

papers.title: From LLMs to MLLMs to Agents: A Survey of Emerging Paradigms in Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses within LLM Ecosystem
papers.journal: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly evolving from single-modal systems to multimodal LLMs and intelligent agents, expanding their capabilities while introducing new security risks. This paper presents a systematic survey of the complexity of jailbreak attacks and defense mechanisms within the expanding LLM ecosystem. We first trace the developmental trajectory from LLMs to MLLMs and Agents, highlighting the core security challenges emerging at each stage. Next, we categorize mainstream jailbreak techniques from the attack impact and attacker permissions perspectives, and provide comprehensive analysis of representative attack methods, related datasets, and evaluation metrics. On the defense side, we organize existing strategies based on response timing and technical approach, offering a structured understanding of their implementation. Furthermore, we identify key limitations in existing surveys, such as insufficient attention to agent-specific security issues, absence of a clear taxonomy for hybrid jailbreak methods, lack of detailed analysis of experimental setups, and outdated coverage of recent advancements. To address these limitations, we provide an updated synthesis of recent work and introduce future research directions in areas such as dataset construction, evaluation framework optimization, and strategy generalization. Our study aims to deepen the understanding of jailbreak mechanisms and promote the development of adaptive defenses for LLMs.

papers.title: Gene tree conflict between genomic and functional partitions impacts phylogenetic inference in Zygophylloideae
authors: P. DE WET VAN DER MERWE
papers.abstract: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic relationships of Zygophylloideae have been analysed in several studies using Sanger sequenced markers, but none have been able to resolve all deeper relationships between genera in the subfamily. Here, we use ion semi-conductor sequencing of chloroplast and nuclear ribosomal regions to analyse these relationships and assess why they have proved so challenging to resolve. We sequenced 39 chloroplast genes and nuclear ribosomal 18S, 5.8S, and 26S genes and internal transcribed spacers (ITS) for key species of Zygophyllum sensu stricto, Roepera, Tetraena, Fagonia , Zygophyllum stapffii and monotypic Augea capensis ; and Tribulus of the subfamily Tribuloideae as outgroup. We aligned these with data from published chloroplast genomes followed by phylogenetic analyses using Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian approaches, summarising phylogenetic results separately for non-coding introns and intergenic spacers, and for genes that are, or are not, involved in photosynthesis. We combined the chloroplast data with sequences of three highly variable noncoding chloroplast regions used in previous studies of greater numbers of taxa, and similarly the nuclear ribosomal data with more densely sampled ITS sequences and assessed whether adding such data resulted in improved support for consistent topologies. We used a chloroplast sequence matrix to infer a dated phylogeny. Adding data did not always improve phylogenetic resolution which was apparently impacted by non-informative variation in chloroplast photosynthesis related genes as well as by conflicting chloroplast and nuclear signals. Chloroplast genes not related to photosynthesis provide robust support for a topology that is consistent with independent data and may therefore represent a useful species tree hypothesis. The cause of the gene tree conflicts remains unclear: potential explanations include functional constraints in photosynthesis related genes and introgressive hybridization and/or incomplete lineage sorting during an ancient rapid divergence. Further testing will require a broader sampling of lineages with different photosynthetic modes and multiple informative, independent, and selectively neutral gene trees.

papers.title: Sulfur-Induced Lattice Disordering in Halide Electrolytes Enables Superionic Sodium-Ion Conduction
papers.abstract: Abstract Amorphous solid electrolytes provide a promising route to overcoming the ion-transport limitations of crystalline halide frameworks, yet achieving superionic Na+ conduction remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-anion amorphous Na-ion solid-state electrolyte, TaCl5-0.5Na2S (NTSC), synthesized via high-energy ball-milling, which exhibits an ultrahigh room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm and a low activation energy of 0.276 eV. Structural analyses reveal a highly disordered framework composed of Ta-centered bipolyhedra interconnected via corner-sharing sulfur atoms [Ta2Cl10S], [TaCl5S], [TaCl4S], and [TaCl4S2], evidenced by comprehensive characterizations, forming a flexible, disordered amorphous network. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations identify continuous Na+-diffusion pathways with low migration barriers. Complementary topological analyses further indicate that sulfur incorporation leads to local lattice distortions, shortens Na–Na hopping distances, and enhances framework flexibility, collectively enabling fast, multidimensional Na+ transport. When applied in all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries (ASSNIBs), NTSC enables high reversible capacity (111.95 mAh/g with a Coulombic efficiency of 92.6% at 0.1 C) and excellent cycling stability (76.9% initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.2 C) at room temperature. This work establishes mixed-anion amorphization as an effective design strategy for high-performance Na-ion solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Terahertz field driven nonlinear Hall effect and other second order transport phenomena in two-dimensional tellurene
papers.abstract: We study terahertz field-driven second-order nonlinear electron transport phenomena, including the nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE), in two-dimensional tellurene flakes. The dc current excited by linearly polarized terahertz (THz) radiation in Hall bar samples is investigated in directions both along and perpendicular to the $c$-axis of tellurene. As expected for second-order transport phenomena, the current scales as the square of the in-plane electric field of the radiation $\bf E$, and depends on its orientation. The current results from a combination of three contributions, including the NLHE, the Nonlinear Longitudinal (NLL) and Nonlinear Diagonal (NLD) currents. We established the equivalence between NLH, NLL, and NLD transport currents and Linear photogalvanic effect (LPGE) contributions induced by the absorption of linearly polarized and unpolarized THz radiation. All contributions can be controlled by a gate voltage and have opposite signs for electron and hole conductivity. The magnitude of the current increases drastically when the samples are cooled from room temperature to 4.2 K. It also increases with decreasing radiation frequency. These results are well described by the developed phenomenological and microscopic theories. We show that the THz radiation-induced electric current originates from microscopic mechanisms such as skew scattering, side jump, and the Berry curvature dipole.

papers.title: Internal Dimethyl Carbonate Circulation-Promoted Synergistic Co-Recycling of Polycarbonates and Polyesters in Methanol
papers.abstract: Abstract Co-recycling of mixed plastic streams offers a viable opportunity to manage spent plastic mixtures and realize a circular economy. Herein, we present an internal dimethyl carbonate (DMC) circulation-promoted co-recycling of polycarbonate (PC) and polyester mixture into their monomers in methanol under mild conditions (e.g., 120 °C). In this protocol, PC is first methanolized to generate DMC and diol under the catalysis of ionic liquids (e.g., 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([BMIm][Cl])), and the resultant DMC participates in the subsequent degradation of polyester over the same catalyst, yielding dimethyl ester and carbonate. Furthermore, the generated carbonate is quickly converted into DMC under the experimental conditions, thus forming an internal DMC circulation. This strategy can be employed in handling mixtures of PC and polyester with various ratios using methanol, affording corresponding monomers in high yields. It provides an innovative perspective that accelerates the development of co-recycling technology for mixed plastic wastes.

papers.title: Thermochemistry of the Water Splitter SrTi0.5Mn0.5O3−δ Studied Using Density Functional Theory (DFT+ U )
papers.abstract: Abstract SrTi0.5Mn0.5O3 (STM55) perovskite has been proven experimentally to be a promising material for hydrogen production using thermochemical water splitting. However, optimizing the performance of STM55 in this application requires a synergistic study of its thermochemical properties using both experiments and computations. In particular, there are several questions with regard to its crystal structure, magnetic ordering, electronic structure, and, more importantly, its off-stoichiometry variation as a function of temperature and oxygen chemical potential. Herein, we tackle these questions employing density functional theory calculations equipped with onsite Hubbard (U) terms applied to Mn and Ti 3d states. This study revealed that STM55 behaves electronically as a metal and is best modeled as a ferromagnet in the pm-3m crystal structure. Oxygen vacancy creation is controlled by the Mn4+/Mn3+ redox couple with minor intervention from Ti cations. Upon a thorough analysis, we selected a set of U parameters (UMn = 3 eV and UTi = 5 eV) that reasonably predict the oxide thermodynamic stability, the oxide off-stoichiometry variations with temperature and oxygen partial pressure, and the temperature dependence of the enthalpy of reduction in the dilute defect regime. Our work furnishes grounds for future extension of our predictive thermodynamic modeling to the nondilute regime by including defect–defect interactions and has general implications for the thermochemistry of the class of metallic oxides.

papers.title: Synergistic regulation of electron and phonon transport in SrTiO 3 -based thermoelectric perovskites via entropy engineering of A-site cations
papers.abstract: Abstract SrTiO3-based thermoelectric oxides are promising candidates for high-temperature energy conversion because of their low cost, environmental compatibility, and excellent thermal stability. However, their relatively low thermoelectric performance remains a key limitation to practical applications. In this work, a series of multicomponent A-site medium- and high-entropy perovskite oxides, (Sr1/2Ba1/4Ca1/4)1-x(La1/3Nd1/3Sm1/3)xTiO3 (SBC-REx; x = 0.08–0.18), were developed to simultaneously regulate electron and phonon transport. All samples maintain a cubic SrTiO3 perovskite phase with Pm–3m symmetry and homogeneous elemental distribution. The doping of La3+, Nd3+ and Sm3+ electron donors modulates the electron carrier concentration, thereby increasing electrical conductivity while preserving moderate carrier mobility and effective mass, leading to enhanced power factor at x = 0.14. Meanwhile, entropy engineering via co-incorporation of multielement rare earth cations in the A-site induces chemical disorder, local lattice distortion and strain fields, which suppress grain growth and intensify phonon scattering, leading to reduced lattice thermal conductivity. Consequently, the optimized SBC-RE0.14 sample achieves a power factor of 1.24 mW m−1 K−2 and thermal conductivity of 3.08 W m−1 K−1, reaching a maximum ZT of 0.31 at 773 K. This work demonstrates that A-site entropy engineering offers an effective strategy to balance electron and phonon transport in SrTiO3-based oxide thermoelectrics.

papers.title: Walkability and Mobility in the Historic District of Nizwa, Oman: A Space Syntax and Multi-Indicator Assessment for Heritage-Led Urban Regeneration
papers.abstract: The issue of walkability in hot, arid heritage cities is still very much under-theorized, as the traditional configurational frameworks have been developed in temperate environments where the thermal barrier and vehicular encroachment do not dominate spatial network logic. This study aims at filling this gap by performing the first quantitative configuration experience coupling test for an Omani historic city, Nizwa. We combine DepthmapX v0.8 Space Syntax analysis of an axial map (428 lines, 612 nodes; eight configurational indicators) of a 1.32 km² area with a validated MAPS-Global/Gehl perceptual audit of 11 purposively sampled streets in four functional zones and 42 semi-structured stakeholder interviews using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. The statistical coupling uses Pearson correlation and OLS regression (Bonferroni corrected α = 0.0009) and a weighted Composite Walkability Index (CWI, max 50). The organic historic fabric shows good syntactic coherence (Connectivity–Integration r = 0.91, p < 0.001; configurational family r = 0.80–0.91), which indicates a well-developed pedestrian network. However, only 19% of the variance in Safety can be accounted for by Global Integration, and 2% of the variance in Accessibility (R² = 0.19 and 0.02 respectively); given the small street sample (n = 11), these associations are exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory and show a critical configuration-experience decoupling (Decoupling Index DI = 0.81) fueled by thermal exclusion, vehicular encroachment, and universal-design deficits. CWI scores range from S2 (Excellent) to S10 (Critical) and the paradigmatic S1 anomaly (second-highest Integration and second-lowest CWI) directly illustrates the decoupling phenomenon. Five evidence-based, heritage-sensitive, costed interventions are proposed in line with Oman Vision 2040 and UN SDG 11.2/11.4; a scenario-based projection suggests a potential 40-74% increase in CWI in the poorest performing streets, at less than 8% of the cost of the conventional masterplan, though this range should be read as an illustrative planning estimate pending simulation-based or post-occupancy validation rather than a guaranteed outcome. The resulting Decoupling Index is a transferable diagnostic tool for hot-arid heritage cores outside of Nizwa.

papers.title: Triggering biodegradation of PLA and PBAT blend films by microembossing
papers.abstract: Abstract In the present work, mechanical embossing with microstamps is used to support biodegradation of PLA/PBAT blends. Films of PLA/PBAT are modified by a microembossing process, using metallic stamps with different surfaces. Subsequently, biodegradation is carried out by incubation with Bacillus subtilis DSM 10. The biodegradation efficiency is evaluated through comparative LSM, WLI, mass loss measurements, as well as ATR-FTIR, Raman microscopy, XRD, REM, DSC and EDX before and after the bioegradation process. Results show that the structuring process leads to a significant increase in the degradation rate of the investigated PLA/PBAT blend. The results can be explained by a relative enrichment of PBAT in the near-surface region after degradation, indicating that the PLA component is preferentially degraded through enzymatic cleavage and subsequent microbial metabolization. The findings further demonstrate that the structure-modified surface enables a deliberately tunable PLA/PBAT film interaction with water: the surface exhibits hydrophobic static wettability alongside a controllable pinning effect during use, while a marked improvement in biodegradation is achieved when brought in contact with microorganisms. Mechanical structuring thus represents a simple, chemical-free, and industrially scalable approach to controlling this dual behavior.

papers.title: Preparation, Optimization and Characterization of Ready‐To‐Eat Puree‐Based Complementary Baby Food
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Apple‐millet complementary baby foods were optimized using apple puree with finger millet or pearl millet flours at ratios ranging from 90:10–60:40. The millets underwent soaking, germination, roasting, and milling, while the apples were blanched and pureed for formulation. Evaluations covered physicochemical evaluation, antioxidants, phenolics, color, texture, thermal stability, FTIR spectra, vitamin C, mineral profiling and nine‐point hedonic sensory scores. Millet incorporation enhanced ash content, antioxidant activity, and phenolics while lowering moisture, total soluble solids, and sensory scores. AFM4 (apple‐finger millet 90:10) and APM4 (apple‐pearl millet 90:10) excelled with favorable texture, acceptable color, and sensory scores matching control. FTIR analysis confirmed that there were no undesirable structural changes to the food matrix after formulation and processing; the major functional groups were retained. DSC‐TGA analysis showed that the chemicals were stable and safe to use as nutrient‐rich baby supplements, while the mineral profiling showed that the product has an adequate amount of mineral content.

papers.title: Sjögren’s disease complicated by TAFRO syndrome: a case report of fever and lymphadenopathy with literature review
papers.abstract: TAFRO syndrome, a fulminant subtype of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease (iMCD), is characterized by thrombocytopenia, anasarca, fever, reticulin fibrosis, renal dysfunction, and organomegaly. Its occurrence in patients with pre-existing Sjögren's disease (SjD) is rare and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. A 59-year-old male with a 10-year history of SjD complicated by primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) presented with a 3-month history of recurrent epistaxis, fever, and lymphadenopathy. Laboratory findings revealed severe thrombocytopenia, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, and positive anti-SSA/Ro and AMA-M2 antibodies. PET-CT demonstrated generalized lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and bilateral pleural effusions. An extensive workup excluded infection, lymphoma, and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Excisional lymph node biopsy confirmed Castleman disease (plasmacytic type), and integration of clinical and pathological findings established the diagnosis of TAFRO syndrome. The patient failed to respond to high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and dexamethasone combined with ruxolitinib. Definitive disease control was ultimately achieved with the RPAD chemotherapy regimen (rituximab, bortezomib, doxorubicin, and dexamethasone), leading to sustained clinical remission with normalized platelet count at 12-month follow-up. This case highlights that TAFRO syndrome can arise on the background of chronic autoimmune disease as a life-threatening cytokine storm, and may be mistaken for refractory HLH. Early recognition through systematic exclusion of mimics and histological confirmation is essential. In patients who fail conventional and cytokine-directed therapies, intensive multi-agent chemotherapy such as the RPAD regimen may be an effective salvage option.

papers.title: Flame retardancy, mechanical, and viscoelastic properties of GFRP composites filled with aluminium tri-hydroxide and ammonium polyphosphate
papers.abstract: Glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) composites are widely used in transportation and structural applications because of their high specific strength, corrosion resistance, and design flexibility. However, the flammability of the GFRP matrix limits its application at elevated temperatures. This study aimed to improve the flame retardancy of GFRP by adding aluminium tri-hydroxide (ATH), ammonium polyphosphate (APP), and hybrid ATH/APP combinations into an unsaturated polyester (UP) resin matrix. The effects of filler addition were evaluated through fire reaction testing, thermal characterization, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), flexural testing, morphological observation, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Fourteen composite variants were fabricated via hand lay-up and press processing: unfilled GFRP as the control, single-filler GFRP containing 10 wt% to 50 wt% ATH or APP, and three hybrid ATH/APP. The +ATH50, +ATH40+APP5, +ATH40+APP10, and +ATH50+APP5 showed that the flame was extinguished before reaching the reference mark used to initiate the measurement of the burning length and time, resulting in a burning rate of 0 mm/min. The SEM observation of the burned surfaces revealed that the hybrid ATH/APP composites formed a thicker and more continuous protective barrier layer than the single-filler composites. The TGA results showed that the maximum mass loss temperature (T max ) of the hybrid ATH/APP composites was higher than that of the single-filler composites, supported by a lower derivative mass change (DMC) relative to unfilled GFRP. The hybrid ATH/APP combination increased T max by up to 16.3%. DSC measurements indicated that this increase in T max was primarily attributed to endothermic heat absorption during ATH decomposition, while APP likely contributed by enhancing the formation of protective barriers. Flexural test results showed that although filler loadings above 40 wt% generally reduced flexural strength, +ATH40+APP5 showed the smallest reduction relative to unfilled GFRP. The DMA results further showed that +ATH40+APP5 possessed the highest storage modulus, loss modulus, and tan δ among the hybrid composites, indicating good resistance to dynamic loading and elevated temperature. Overall, +ATH40+APP5 provided the best balance of flame retardancy, thermal stability, and mechanical performance for structural GFRP applications.

The DMA results further showed that +ATH40+APP5 possessed the highest storage modulus, loss modulus, and tan δ among the hybrid composites, indicating good resistance to dynamic loading and elevated temperature. Overall, +ATH40+APP5 provided the best balance of flame retardancy, thermal stability, and mechanical performance for structural GFRP applications.

papers.title: Real‐World Use of Rezafungin for the Treatment of Challenging Aspergillus Infections
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aspergillus infections can pose significant treatment challenges, due in part to increasing triazole resistance. Clinical insight is needed to understand the potential for rezafungin, a next-generation echinocandin with once-weekly dosing, to address some limitations of current treatments for Aspergillus infections. METHODS: This retrospective case series collected anonymized real-world data from eight adults who received once-weekly rezafungin for difficult-to-treat Aspergillus infections. The cases were provided by clinicians in Spain, the UK, and Italy with considerable experience in treating challenging fungal infections. RESULTS: Most patients had pulmonary aspergillosis, nearly all had failed or were intolerant to triazole-based regimens, and half had prior echinocandin or amphotericin B exposure. Rezafungin was used primarily to enable outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT), avoiding the need for daily IV echinocandin in settings of azole resistance or intolerance. About half received rezafungin as monotherapy; others had combination regimens. Clinical and/or radiological improvement or disease stabilization was observed in most cases, including in patients with azole-resistant infections. Notably, one patient achieved resolution of chronic otitis media, and others had negative cultures or sustained clinical benefit. Rezafungin was well tolerated, including in patients with renal impairment. One patient with chronic aspergilloma did not achieve adequate symptomatic control with rezafungin and required surgery. CONCLUSIONS: This report provides initial clinical insights on rezafungin as a potential option for difficult-to-treat Aspergillus infections. In this limited group of patients, rezafungin enabled OPAT, facilitated hospital discharge, and provided clinically meaningful improvements, including prolonged disease stabilization and resolution, which merit further investigation in clinical trials.

papers.title: Qingqiao polyphenols may alleviate multi-organ inflammatory injury caused by Escherichia coli infection in chickens by regulating pyroptosis in a gut microbiota-independent manner
papers.abstract: Background This study systematically elucidates the mechanism by which Qingqiao polyphenols (QP) alleviate bacterial infectious lesions in poultry by regulating the pyroptosis signaling pathway. Methods An Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) O157 infection model was established and evaluate the effect of QP on infected chickens. Results Results showed QP significantly alleviated infection-induced systemic damage, manifested as improved pathological lesions in liver and lungs, and restored mucosal structures in duodenum, jejunum, and ileum. Further studies demonstrated that QP alleviates inflammatory damage in the liver, lungs, and intestines (duodenum, jejunum, ileum) of chickens induced by E. coli , by suppressing the pyroptosis signaling pathway. After gut microbial depletion by antibiotics, a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced chicken enteritis model was used to evaluate whether QP can exert anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting the pyroptosis pathway. The results demonstrated that QP effectively suppressed pyroptosis and alleviated LPS-induced intestinal inflammation, maintaining efficacy even under antibiotic depleted microbiota group conditions. This suggests that the anti-inflammatory effect of QP may be mediated by a pyroptosis pathway that is independent of the gut microbiota. Conclusion This study confirms that QP exerts multi-organ protective effects against E. coli -induced inflammatory injury via a gut microbiota-independent pyroptosis-inhibitory mechanism, which provides a new theoretical basis for the application of QP as an antibiotic substitute in poultry bacterial disease prevention and control.

papers.title: Functionalization of Carbon Nanotubes with 5-Phenylvaleryl, Pentadecanoyl, and Adipoyl Chloride: Synthesis and Spectroscopic Surface Analysis Toward Biomarker Sensing
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were covalently modified with aromatic (5-phenylvaleryl, 5PC), long-chain aliphatic (pentadecanoyl, PDC), and oxygen-rich/carboxylated (adipoyl, ACC) chemistries to create a tunable surface interface for detecting volatile and semivolatile chemical biomarkers. Following oxidative activation, 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) amination, and acyl-chloride coupling, successful attachment and differentiation of linker classes were evaluated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS), and C KLL Auger analysis. Distinct spectroscopic fingerprints corresponding to aromatic, aliphatic, and oxygenated functionalities were resolved despite the intrinsically carbon-rich substrate. These orthogonal signatures provide a compact quality-control strategy for CNT functionalization and establish a framework for correlating surface chemistry with predicted analyte interactions, including aromatic interactions, nonpolar adsorption, and acid–base or hydrogen-bond pairing. This surface chemistry palette is intended to enable flexible CNT-based sensor arrays for noninvasive monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers, including ketones associated with diabetes, nitrogen-containing species linked to chronic kidney disease, and volatile compounds implicated in preictal seizure states. Sensor-level performance was not evaluated in the present study and is the subject of ongoing device work.

papers.title: Response surface optimization, morphological characterization, and thermal analysis of bamboo-based composite biomass pellets
papers.journal: Journal of the Chinese Institute of Engineers
papers.abstract: Bamboo-based composite biomass pellets were prepared using bamboo sawdust as the base material and incorporating camphor leaves and maize straw. Maize-straw composition was literature-derived, not experimentally measured. Single-factor tests and a Box–Behnken response surface design assessed how molding temperature, wet-basis moisture content, and blending ratio affected pellet density and compressive strength. SEM supported morphological interpretation; TG/DTG served as supplementary, unreplicated thermal characterization rather than an optimization response. Temperature had the largest statistical effect on density, while temperature and camphor leaf content most strongly influenced compressive strength. Higher temperature and appropriate moisture promoted compactness, reduced pore defects, and improved structural continuity. A process-robust condition of 178°C, 8.3% moisture content, 27% wb camphor leaves, and 21% wb maize straw gave predicted density and compressive strength of 1.28 g·cm−3 and 3.401 MPa, respectively. Experimental validation yielded 1.197 ± 0.027 g·cm−3 and 3.133 ± 0.220 MPa (mean ± SE, n = 3), with relative prediction errors of 6.51% and 7.87%, respectively. TG/DTG descriptively confirmed typical staged lignocellulosic decomposition. These results provide a practical basis for optimizing bamboo-based multi-feedstock pelletization.
papers.summary: Bamboo-based composite biomass pellets were prepared using bamboo sawdust as the base material and incorporating camphor leaves and maize straw. TG/DTG descriptively confirmed typical staged lignocellulosic decomposition. These results provide a practical basis for optimizing bamboo-based multi-feedstock pelletization.

papers.title: Research Progress and Clinical Translational Application of Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Microcirculation Imaging
papers.journal: Advanced ultrasound in diagnosis and therapy
papers.abstract: Abstract As an emerging super-resolution ultrasound imaging technology, ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) breaks the acoustic diffraction limit of conventional ultrasound. By localizing and tracking individual microbubble contrast agents at the sub-wavelength scale, ULM achieves high-precision visualization and quantitative evaluation of micron-level microvascular structures and hemodynamic parameters. Compared with traditional color Doppler flow imaging and contrast-enhanced ultrasound, ULM possesses superior spatial resolution and microcirculation quantification capability, enabling in-depth analysis of microvascular morphological remodeling and functional perfusion abnormalities. This review summarizes the core technical principles, optimized algorithms, and key technical bottlenecks of ULM, including microbubble signal separation, single-bubble localization accuracy, physiological motion artifacts, and prolonged acquisition duration. Furthermore, we comprehensively elaborate the preclinical and clinical application progress of ULM in multiple systems, covering neurovascular, renal, tumor, cardiovascular, endocrine and cardiac microcirculation diseases, with a specific focus on its novel clinical value in identifying vulnerable carotid atherosclerotic plaques. We also discuss the current limitations restricting large-scale clinical translation, standardized protocol establishment, and deep-tissue imaging performance of ULM, noting that the majority of existing human ULM evidence is still at the feasibility stage and large-scale prospective multi-center clinical validations are still needed. Targeting the above-mentioned translational bottlenecks, finally, this review prospects the future development directions of ULM, including artificial intelligence optimization, three-dimensional whole-organ imaging, multi-modal and multi-omics fusion. With continuous technical iteration, ULM is expected to become a novel non-invasive imaging modality for early diagnosis, risk stratification and therapeutic efficacy evaluation of microcirculation-related disorders.

papers.title: Long-Term Performance of Biofilters Packed with Manure-Derived Media for Trimethylamine Removal: Operational Responses and Microbial Succession
papers.abstract: Four laboratory-scale biofilters were designed and evaluated for treating trimethylamine (TMA). Each biofilter was measured as being 68 cm in height and 15 cm in diameter. The filter media consisted of various mixtures of dairy manure compost, dairy barn bedding, crushed corn cobs, wood chips, and sawdust. This study aimed to compare the removal efficiencies of TMA achieved by biofilters packed with different media compositions, as well as to analyze the succession patterns in the structure of microbial communities on the media surfaces during operation. Contaminated air streams were artificially generated by bubbling air through a TMA solution, resulting in inlet concentrations ranging from 1.88 to 4.23 mg/m3. Under empty bed residence times (EBRTs) ranging from 42.7 to 28.0 s, all four biofilters achieved removal efficiencies exceeding 60%. However, the performance varied among the biofilters. The biofilter packed with a mixture of matured compost, wood chips, and crushed corn cobs at a volume ratio of 10:9:1 exhibited the highest removal efficiency (>83%). Ammonia was detected at the outlet of the biofilters as a byproduct of microbial TMA degradation, accompanied by the accumulation of ammonium nitrogen in the filter media. Microbial community analysis of the high-performance biofilter revealed a progressive increase in microbial complexity and diversity over 95 days of operation. Glycomyces was the dominant genus throughout the operation and showed a significant positive association with TMA removal efficiency, but its specific role in TMA degradation remains to be experimentally confirmed.

Microbial community analysis of the high-performance biofilter revealed a progressive increase in microbial complexity and diversity over 95 days of operation. papers.title: Emerging role of nuclear phospholipase C-β1 in lung cancer
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a highly aggressive malignancy accounting for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases. To better understand its pathology and prognosis, this study focused on the molecular profiling of tissues and clinical outcomes derived directly from lung cancer patients. Recently, the involvement of phospholipase enzymes in cancer has been highlighted, as they are involved in crucial cellular signaling pathways. The mRNA and protein expression levels of phospholipase C (PLC) isoforms were analyzed in biopsies from NSCLC patients. Utilizing Kaplan-Meier plotter database, the prognostic role of PLCs could be assessed. Researchers identified significant changes in mRNA and protein expression levels of various PLC isoforms in patient biopsies. Notably, PLCβ1 was found to be overexpressed in every tumor sample. In addition, the use of KM-Plotter hypothesized an association between elevated PLCβ1 levels and poorer survival outcomes, emphasizing the variations due to patient-specific factors, such as tumor stage and smoking history. Immunohistochemistry performed on patient-derived samples revealed a clear contrast in protein localization. In tumor tissues, PLCβ1 was predominantly found in the nucleus, whereas in adjacent healthy tissues, it remained almost exclusively in the cytoplasm. Nuclear localization is known to be linked to cell cycle modulation; therefore, it may represent a critical event in cancer development. The study highlighted critical alterations in PLC isoforms observed within the patient population. These findings demonstrate that PLCβ1 is significantly upregulated in malignant tissues and correlates with adverse clinical outcomes. Consequently, PLCβ1 may serve as a candidate biomarker, warranting further investigation into its potential role in the management and treatment of NSCLC patients.

papers.title: Switching between semaglutide and tirzepatide in obesity Management: an expert-consensus framework for approximate clinical Efficacy-matched switching doses
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Currently, there are no available guidelines for switching from semaglutide to tirzepatide, since the mechanisms of action and pharmacokinetics differ, thus posing a challenge for continuous treatment of obesity. AREAS COVERED: A narrative review of PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov (to May 2026) evaluated trials and cohorts comparing semaglutide (0.25-7.2 mg) and tirzepatide (2.5-15 mg). We synthesized indirect treatment comparisons to outline dose-response relationships and develop approximate Efficacy-matched switching doses bands. EXPERT OPINION: Estimation of clinical Efficacy-matched switching doses is more practical than mandatory lowest-dose initiation, which naturally risks a 'therapeutic gap' and subsequent weight regain. Until prospective switching trials validate exact conversions, clinicians should utilize the proposed equivalence bands and the 5-step clinical decision algorithm to guide seamless transitions, titrating doses every 4-8 weeks based on individual tolerability and metabolic outcomes.

papers.title: VLM-based multi-agent architecture for multifunctional robotic health attendant (RHA) using phase-prompt task design
papers.abstract: Introduction Healthcare robots are increasingly needed to support clinicians whose work involves diverse tasks and frequent task switching. However, most healthcare robots developed to assist clinicians either perform a single function or implement multiple functions as fixed task pipelines that are difficult to adapt to different patients, rooms, or care teams. This study presents a vision language model (VLM) based multiagent architecture for a multifunctional Robotic Health Attendant (RHA). Methods In this architecture, each task can be designed by writing natural language phase specifications that describe how available tools should be used during task execution. A main agent interprets natural language requests from clinicians or patients and routes each request to the appropriate task agent. During execution, the VLM uses language, visual input, and contextual information to select tools and interpret their results. A shared Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool layer provides elemental robot functions such as navigation, manipulation, and perception across tasks. The architecture was implemented on a TIAGo Pro robot and evaluated in an unoccupied patient room across five tasks including object delivery, documentation, visual monitoring, patient education, and medication reminders. Results The case study demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed architecture as a reasoning core for a multifunctional healthcare robot by executing multiple tasks and adapting task behavior by editing natural language phase specifications. The comparison across three VLMs showed that longer tool-call sequences led to skipped steps and, in some cases, false reports of task success, which is a key reliability concern for healthcare robots performing long, multi-step tasks. Discussion The study also identified technical limitations and future research needs that must be addressed to make the architecture more robust in realistic care settings.

papers.title: Evolutionary and Neurobiological Determinants of Exploratory Behaviour in Domestic Dog (Canis familiaris): Insights from Selected Hunting Breed Groups
papers.abstract: The aim of this review is to summarize current knowledge on the evolutionary and neurobiological determinants of exploratory behaviour in the domestic dog (Canis familiaris) and to examine how these processes are reflected in the exploratory strategies of selected hunting breed groups classified within FCI Groups VI, VII, and VIII. The influence of domestication and long-term artificial selection on the development of behavioural traits, socio-cognitive abilities, and sensory predispositions of modern dog breeds is discussed. Particular attention is given to the neurobiological mechanisms underlying exploratory behaviour, including the roles of the reward system, hippocampus, olfactory pathways, and brain structures involved in emotional regulation. The roles of olfactory, visual, and auditory sensory systems in exploratory behaviour are discussed, and commonly used methods for its assessment, including the Open Field Test (OFT) and the Free Choice paradigm, are reviewed. Special emphasis is placed on behavioural variation among breeds belonging to FCI Groups VI, VII, and VIII. These groups represent distinct exploratory strategies shaped by their historical working functions, ranging from predominantly olfactory-based exploration in scent hounds, through active searching of open environments in pointing dogs, to multimodal exploration of terrestrial and aquatic environments in retrievers, flushing dogs, and water dogs. The practical implications of exploratory behaviour for canine welfare in contemporary human environments are also discussed. The available evidence indicates that exploratory behaviour in dogs arises from the interaction of evolutionary adaptations, neurobiological mechanisms, and functional selection, while the diversity of exploratory strategies observed among hunting breed groups reflects their historical working specialization.

papers.title: Jiangshui-derived Lactobacillus plantarum GR-4 enhances the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors against gastric cancer
papers.abstract: Objective To investigate whether the Jiangshui-derived probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum GR-4 can enhance gastric cancer sensitivity to PD-1 inhibitors and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment. Methods A mouse gastric cancer model was established. Mice received oral GR-4 monotherapy, PD-1 blocking antibody monotherapy, or combined GR-4 and PD-1 antibody treatment. In vivo antitumor efficacy was evaluated by measuring tumor weight. We assessed CD8 + T-cell infiltration, cytokines related to T-cell activation and differentiation, and the expression of the activation marker CD69 on CD3 + /CD8 + T cells within tumor tissues. 16S rRNA sequencing of gut microbiota and fecal metabolomic analysis were performed to explore the regulatory effects of GR-4 on gut microbiota composition and metabolic profiles. In vitro , human gastric cancer BGC-823 cells were treated with GR-4 combined with PD-1 intervention, and transcriptome sequencing was applied to further validate the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms. Results In vivo results demonstrated that combined GR-4 and PD-1 antibody treatment exerted prominent synergistic antitumor activity, effectively suppressing tumor growth while markedly mitigating PD-1-associated body weight loss (p < 0.01). Further assays revealed that GR-4 synergistically elevated tumor-infiltrating CD3 + /CD8 + T-cell levels and upregulated CD69 expression on these cells, thereby remodelling the tumor immune microenvironment. Additionally, GR-4, whether administered alone or combined with PD-1 antibody, optimized gut microbiota structure, increased the abundance of probiotic genera including Ligilactobacillus and Bacteroides , reversed intestinal metabolic disturbances, and raised the levels of short-chain fatty-acid-related metabolites such as ethoxyacetic acid and 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid. Transcriptomic sequencing showed significant enrichment of the PD-1 checkpoint pathway in the GR-4 group versus Ctrl (p=0.01), whereas no significant enrichment was observed between the PD-1 inhibitor group and GR-4/PD-1 inhibitor group (p=0.14). Conclusion This study is the first to confirm that Lactobacillus plantarum GR-4 synergizes with PD-1 inhibitors to restrain gastric cancer progression via T-cell activation and elevated intratumoral T-cell infiltration. These findings provide novel theoretical evidence and a potential combinatorial immunotherapeutic strategy for gastric cancer.

papers.title: High-Throughput Synthesis and Screening of Cyclometalated Iridium Complexes for Antibacterial Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract The discovery of novel antibiotics to address the rise of antimicrobial resistance is an increasingly pressing issue for global health. In recent years, transition-metal complexes have gained attention as potential antibacterial agents. We herein describe a new methodology to generate novel cyclometalated iridium compounds with bidentate Schiff ligands in a high-throughput combinatorial approach, alongside the expansion of an existing approach using bidentate pyridine-triazole ligands, with the aim of finding new metalloantibiotics. A total of 552 new complexes were synthesized and evaluated. Variety in the libraries was introduced by including three cyclometalating phenylpyridine ligands, demonstrating that the synthesis can tolerate both electron-rich and electron-poor metal scaffolds while using mild and biologically compatible conditions. Screening of the crude reaction mixtures in a direct-to-biology approach revealed a number of highly active complexes against Gram-positive bacteria, which was confirmed by resynthesis and further testing of lead compounds. This approach widens the scope of metal complex combinatorial chemistry, enabling rapid exploration of the chemical space involving cyclometalated iridium complexes.

papers.title: Biopolymer‐Enhanced PAAc / PAAm Hydrogels: Impact of Carrageenan Incorporation on Structure, Functionality, and Adsorption Behavior for Wastewater Remediation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(acrylic acid‐co‐acrylamide) (PAAc/PAAm) and carrageenan incorporated PAAc/PAAm (CAR/PAAc/PAAm) hydrogels were synthesized via free‐radical polymerization using sodium persulfate as a chemical initiator. The effect of carrageenan incorporation on the structural, thermal, swelling, and adsorption properties of the hydrogels was systematically investigated. FTIR and XRD analyses confirmed successful network formation and increased amorphous character after carrageenan addition, while TGA demonstrated improved thermal stability. SEM, AFM, and EDX analyses revealed a rougher, more porous surface enriched with sulfate functional groups, providing enhanced adsorption sites. The CAR/PAAc/PAAm hydrogel exhibited higher swelling capacity and pH‐responsive behavior compared with pristine PAAc/PAAm. Adsorption studies using methylene blue (MB) and tartrazine yellow (TY) dyes showed significantly higher removal efficiency and faster adsorption kinetics for the carrageenan‐modified hydrogel. Kinetic and isotherm analyses indicated diffusion‐controlled adsorption for TY and chemisorption‐dominated adsorption for MB, confirming the strong role of carrageenan in enhancing dye uptake. These results demonstrate the potential of CAR/PAAc/PAAm hydrogels as efficient and sustainable adsorbents for wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Performance Assessment of Biocomposite Phase Change Materials for Sustainable Thermal Energy Storage
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel, cost‐effective composite phase change material (PCM) using cetyl alcohol (CAL) and shape‐stabilizing biochar derived from industrial waste wood carbon (WWC) for low‐temperature thermal energy storage, and the simultaneous use of Kissinger and Ozawa techniques to assess the kinetics and activation energies of PCM samples. Biochar content was varied from 0 to 3 g per 10 g CAL to synthesize various composite PCM samples. The morphological studies confirmed the encapsulation of molten PCM into biochar. FTIR and XRD investigations confirmed the chemical stability of the synthesized PCM samples, ascribing to the absence of extra peaks/bands. TGA studies divulged the enhanced thermal stability of the CAL4 sample. CAL4 sample has exhibited suitable thermal properties comprising a latent heat of 184.83 J/g, an encapsulation efficiency of 76.76%, and a thermal energy storage capacity of 99.62%. The activation energy of CAL4 calculated by both models, i.e., 551.118 and 531.827 kJ/mol, is superior compared to that of the pure PCM, which is due to the porous matrix of the CAL4 sample. Even after 100 thermal cycles, CAL4 showed negligible thermal property changes and zero leakage, proving it as a cost‐effective leak‐proof solution for long‐term low‐temperature thermal energy storage applications.

papers.title: Design and Characterization of Fluorinated Maleimide-Based Hybrid Nanofiber Composites as Potential Separators for High-Temperature Batteries
papers.abstract: The development of functional polymeric nanofibers having both superior thermal stability and surface wetting properties simultaneously is a significant research topic in advanced materials engineering. For this purpose, copolymers of 3,5-bis((perfluorophenyl)methoxy)benzyl-4-(2,5-dioxo-2,5-dihydro-1 H-pyrrol-1-yl)benzoate (FMI) with acrylonitrile (AN) and styrene (St) were synthesized via free-radical copolymerization. The molecular weights were determined by gel permeation chromatography (GPC), while structural characterization was conducted via 1H-NMR and Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopies. Hybrid nanofiber membranes of the synthesized polymers were fabricated via electrospinning. Thermal stability was assessed by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), which revealed that the incorporation of maleimide groups significantly improved the thermal stability of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterization showed a distinct morphological trend that the nanofiber diameter systematically decreased with increasing fluorine content. Furthermore, surface wetting investigations revealed that despite the intrinsic hydrophilicity of the baseline PAN matrix, the integration of fluorinated segments imparted pronounced hydrophobic and oleophobic characteristics to the resulting nanofiber networks.

papers.title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I 3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

papers.title: A New Nitrogen–Phosphorus Bio-Based Flame Retardant for Cotton Fabric: Investigation of Combustion Behavior and Fire Safety Parameters
papers.abstract: A bio-based flame retardant, melamine salt of folic phosphate (MFP), was synthesized through a two-step reaction involving phosphoric acid, folic acid, and melamine. The chemical structure of MFP was confirmed using FTIR, 1H NMR, 31P NMR, and XRD analyses. MFP was applied to cotton fabric (CF), resulting in treated samples with weight gains of 10% (CF10) and 20% (CF20). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) results revealed that MFP improved the char yield of CF at 750°C, indicating its effectiveness as a char-forming agent. The CF20 sample exhibited self-extinguishing properties, in a vertical flame test (VFT), with a char length of 10.4 cm. Additionally, the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18.2% in CF to 31.5% in CF20, confirming its transition from a flammable to a flame-resistant material. Cone calorimetry results indicated that the MFP treatment significantly improved the fire safety parameters of the CF. Specifically, the peak of heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (THR) were reduced by 48.9% and 34.3%, respectively, for the CF20 sample compared to the untreated CF. Furthermore, the fire growth index (FGI) decreased from 17 kW/m2 s in the untreated CF to 8.2 kW/m2 s in CF20. Conversely, the fire performance index (FPI) increased from 0.008 m2 s/kW to 0.034 m2 s/kW. The mechanical properties analysis indicated that the tensile strength of the treated samples increased by 2.5% for CF20, while the extension at break exhibited a slight decrease of 15.6%. This work offers a new methodology to engineer fire-safe CF without compromising its inherent material properties.

Cone calorimetry results indicated that the MFP treatment significantly improved the fire safety parameters of the CF.

papers.title: Multifidelity Thermochemical–Mechanical Modeling of Pultruded Hollow Composite Profiles
papers.journal: Journal of Manufacturing Science and Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Pultrusion of hollow composite profiles with fast‐curing polyurethane (PU) resin requires simultaneous control of heat transfer, cure kinetics, viscosity evolution, and pulling resistance, making empirical process optimization costly and uncertain. This work develops a multifidelity thermo–chemical–mechanical modeling framework for hollow glass‐fiber (GF) and carbon‐fiber (CF)‐reinforced PU profiles produced on an industrial PulFlex pultrusion line. Three complementary model tiers are integrated using a common physics backbone: a one‐dimensional (1D) mathematical model for rapid parametric screening, a two‐dimensional (2D) homogeneous finite element model in ABAQUS for process‐scale response, and a three‐dimensional (3D) laminate‐resolved finite element model in ANSYS for fiber‐architecture and through‐thickness gradient prediction. All models employ Kamal–Sourour cure kinetics, Di Benedetto vitrification, cure‐dependent rheology, and cure‐hardening instantaneously linear elastic modulus evolution to predict temperature, degree of cure, viscosity, glass‐transition temperature, and pulling force along a multizone heated die. Embedded thermocouple measurements are used to calibrate the 1D thermal history and to independently evaluate the 2D and 3D thermal predictions at the reference condition, whereas differential scanning calorimetry‐derived degree‐of‐cure data provide an independent check on cure progression for all three model tiers. The models reveal distinct thermochemical behavior between GF and CF systems and quantify the accuracy‐versus‐cost tradeoff across fidelities. Under the tested three‐zone heater configuration, the multifidelity comparison identifies the speed range over which die‐exit cure, vitrification location, and predicted pulling resistance remain favorable for stable hollow‐profile manufacturing. The calibrated 1D model supports efficient process screening and future digital‐twin integration.

papers.title: Atherosclerosis: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Interventions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Atherosclerosis is no longer viewed solely as a lipid‐storage disorder but rather as a complex multisystem inflammatory disease driven by interactions among the vascular, immune, metabolic, and nervous systems. This review integrates recent concepts, including trained immunity, the neuroimmune cardiovascular interface, vascular cell plasticity, and the microbiome–vascular axis, that reshape the understanding of plaque initiation, progression, and instability. We summarize how established lipid‐lowering, antidiabetic, antihypertensive, and revascularization strategies influence atherosclerotic disease and discuss emerging interventions, including RNA therapeutics, anti‐inflammatory agents, gene therapy, and cell‐based approaches. Key ongoing clinical trials that may clarify the cardiovascular benefits and safety of these strategies are also reviewed. Despite therapeutic advances, residual cardiovascular risk persists because of limitations in animal models, sex‐related differences in plaque phenotype, and the lack of clinically applicable biomarkers. Nanotechnology, human microphysiological systems, spatial multiomics, and artificial intelligence may help bridge these translational gaps. Successful clinical implementation will nevertheless require biomarker‐guided patient selection, rational combination therapy, validated surrogate endpoints, long‐term safety assessment, and attention to health economics. In summary, these advances will shape future translational research and clinical trial design, ultimately advancing personalized management of atherosclerosis.

papers.title: 6-Hydroxyrubiadin Regulates TNF-α-Induced MUC5AC Gene Expression via Affecting NF-κB and MAPK Signaling Pathways in Human Airway Epithelial Cells
papers.abstract: Nakai, exerts a regulatory effect on the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin under conditions mimicking pulmonary inflammation in human airway epithelial cells. Confluent NCI-H292 cells were pretreated with 6-HR for 30 min, followed by stimulation with tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α for 24 h. MUC5AC mRNA expression and glycoprotein production were measured using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), respectively. Further, we examined the effect of 6-HR on TNF-α-induced activation of the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways via immunoblot analysis. The results were as follows: (1) 6-HR significantly reduced both the production of MUC5AC glycoprotein and MUC5AC mRNA expression in NCI-H292 cells. (2) 6-HR inhibited TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation through a transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)-dependent mechanism. (3) 6-HR also inhibited TAK1-dependent MAPK signaling pathways activated by TNF-α, resulting in the downregulation of MUC5AC mucin production in NCI-H292 cells. These findings suggest that 6-HR regulates the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin by directly acting on airway epithelial cells through modulation of the MAPK and NF-κB signaling pathways.
