papers.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
papers.abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

papers.title: Building AI (In)dependence through EU’s AI Factories
papers.abstract: This paper analyses the European Union’s flagship initiative to become an international leader in AI: the 19 AI Factories, spread across 16 EU Member States. At the moment, a few large AI companies from the US (‘Big AI’) hold key parts of the AI market. Smaller European startups therefore struggle with barriers to entry, lock-in effects, and dependencies in the global ‘AI race’. The AI Factories try to respond to this – but to what extent can they achieve their high ambitions? By employing a doctrinal analysis of the relevant EU law and semi-structured interviews with nine industry experts (six AI startup representatives, two Big AI representatives, and one AIF representative), the study analyses the capacity of the AI Factories to function as public alternatives to Big AI. Our findings indicate that while the AI Factories – on paper – offer free access for startups to AI-optimised supercomputing, technical support, data services, and regulatory guidance, their real-world impact remains limited at this time. This is mainly due to limited awareness among startups, misalignment with startups’ commercialisation needs, and restrictions that limit AI Factory use to model training rather than deployment. Furthermore, the platform lock-in to Big AI further reduces startups’ willingness to ‘migrate’ and train their models with the AI Factories. The paper concludes that, as of now, the AI Factories alone are unlikely to reduce startups’ reliance on Big AI, but combined with stronger competition enforcement and targeted industrial policy, they could contribute to a more self-reliant European AI system.

papers.title: Acidification and Nutritional Changes During Controlled Fermentation of Bambusa spinosa Roxb. Shoots Using Indigenous Lactic Acid Bacteria
papers.abstract: This study evaluated two indigenous lactic acid bacteria isolates as starter cultures for controlled fermentation of Bambusa spinosa Roxb. shoots. BSISO1 and BSISO14, recovered from fresh B. spinosa Roxb. shoots, were selected based on colony morphology and Gram stain reaction. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing, the isolates were putatively identified as Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BSISO1 and Lactiplantibacillus pentosus BSISO14. Three fermentation treatments were established: BSISO1-inoculated, BSISO14-inoculated, and uninoculated spontaneous fermentation. The inoculated treatments received 3% (v/v) starter culture and were fermented for 14 days. The pH and total titratable acidity (TTA) were monitored every two days, while fat, reducing sugar, protein, and crude fiber were measured at the end of fermentation. Treatment, fermentation day, and their interaction significantly affected acidification. BSISO1 produced the lowest overall pH and highest overall TTA, followed by BSISO14, while spontaneous fermentation showed the weakest acidification. Fermentation markedly reduced reducing sugar and crude fiber relative to fresh shoots, whereas fat remained relatively stable. BSISO14 showed numerically higher protein and crude fiber values than spontaneous fermentation. These results indicate preliminary potential that BSISO1 and BSISO14 can support controlled fermentation of B. spinosa shoots, with BSISO1 showing stronger acidification performance. Further microbial, metabolomic, sensory, safety, and shelf-life evaluations are required before practical starter-culture application.

papers.title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

papers.title: Combining enhanced basalt weathering with soda saline soil: A novel CO₂ mineralisation strategy
papers.abstract: Enhanced rock weathering in saline–alkaline soils can couple CO₂ mineralisation with reclamation of salt-affected land. We incubated 30 g basalt with 30 g sodic saline soil for 90 days at 15 °C using three particle sizes (0.074, 0.42 and 5 mm) and two water additions (30 and 60 g). Endpoint aqueous chemistry, SEM–EDS, thermogravimetric analysis and PHREEQC saturation modelling were integrated with a regional life-cycle assessment for Jilin Province, China. Endpoint Ca accounting yielded apparent weathered-basalt masses, which were converted using a primary Ca-only carbonate capacity of 0.072 g CO₂ g⁻¹ basalt and an all-base-cation carbonate-equivalent upper capacity of 0.142 g CO₂ g⁻¹ basalt. Particle-size-specific effective rates linked the incubation results to 30-year weathering trajectories. Gross CDR reached 72.45–72.47 kg CO₂ t⁻¹ basalt in the primary case and 141.92–141.96 kg CO₂ t⁻¹ basalt in the upper case. Across twelve scenarios, primary-case net CDR ranged from −5.53 to 38.45 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹ basalt, while upper-case net CDR ranged from 63.96 to 107.92 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹ basalt. Net-removal costs ranged from USD 1327–29,328 t⁻¹ CO₂ in the primary net-removing scenarios and from USD 473–4667 t⁻¹ CO₂ in the upper case. The identified 6376,490 ha of Jilin cropland, equivalent to 482.06 Mt basalt at 75.6 t ha⁻¹ , had gross capacities of 34.93 Mt CO₂ (primary) and 68.43 Mt CO₂ (upper). Finer particles reached the composition-controlled capacity sooner, whereas coarse basalt had lower supply-chain emissions in the evaluated scenarios.

papers.title: Synergistic catalytic co-pyrolysis of eucalyptus bark and polyethylene over natural clinoptilolite: Thermogravimetric and kinetic evidence
papers.abstract: Catalytic co-pyrolysis is a promising strategy for thermochemical conversion of biomass and plastic wastes; however, the combined influence of hydrogen-rich polymers and natural zeolite catalysts on reaction kinetics remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and natural clinoptilolite (CLIN) on the thermal degradation behavior, interactions, and apparent activation energies of eucalyptus bark (EB). Thermogravimetric analyses were performed under pyrolysis, catalytic pyrolysis, co-pyrolysis, and catalytic co-pyrolysis conditions at 10, 30, and 50 K min −1 . Interactions were evaluated using the deviation method, while apparent activation energies were determined using the Friedman and Kissinger–Akahira–Sunose (KAS) methods. Co-pyrolysis with LDPE produced composition- and heating-rate-dependent synergistic and inhibitory interactions and reduced the mean apparent activation energies in the lignin/LDPE-dominated region relative to pure LDPE. Clinoptilolite modified the kinetic behavior depending on blend composition and catalyst loading. Catalytic co-pyrolysis of the blend containing 50 wt% LDPE and 15 wt% CLIN exhibited particularly low mean apparent activation energies in Regions I and II, and the highest pyrolysis performance index among catalytic blends at 50 K min −1 . These findings support the potential application of low-cost natural zeolites in biomass–plastic co-pyrolysis.

papers.title: Luminescent Iridium(III) Complex with Alkoxy-Functionalised 2-Phenylpyridine Ligands: Synthesis, Spectroscopic and Photophysical Studies
papers.abstract: Cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes have garnered considerable interest owing to their exceptional photophysical properties and broad applicability in luminescence-based technologies.This work describes the preparation, spectroscopic analysis, and photophysical characterisation of a new emissive iridium(III) complex, [Ir(bFppy)₂(eFppy)], incorporating the ligands 2-(2butoxy-4-fluorophenyl)pyridine (bFppy) and 2-(2-ethoxy-4-fluorophenyl)pyridine (eFppy).The structure identity of the complex was confirmed by ¹H NMR, ¹³C NMR, and FTIR spectroscopic techniques.In the ¹H NMR spectrum, aliphatic proton signals were observed between δ 1.00-4.09ppm, corresponding to the ethyl and butyl chain protons, while signals in the δ 5.99-8.81ppm region were attributed to aromatic protons of the phenylpyridine frameworks.A total of 43 carbon resonances were resolved in the ¹³C NMR spectrum, in complete accordance with the number of carbon atoms anticipated from the proposed structure.Complementary FTIR data supported these assignments through the observation of C-H, C=C, and C=N stretching bands characteristic of the complex.UV-Vis spectroscopy identified π-π* intraligand transitions in the ultraviolet region and MLCT transitions extending into the visible range.Steady-state emission measurements revealed that the complex produces intense green phosphorescence in dichloromethane solution at ambient temperature, with an emission maximum at λem = 502 nm, indicative of an emissive pathway dominated by ³MLCT character.The efficient triplet-state emission exhibited by this complex highlights its promising prospects for applications in optoelectronic devices, such as organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs).

papers.title: Hydraulic behavior and solute redistribution of saline-alkali black soil: Implications for stormwater source control
papers.abstract: Study Region Daqing, northeastern China, has saline-alkali soils, strong evaporation, and shallow groundwater that constrain infiltration-based stormwater source control. Study Focus We examined hydraulic behavior and water and solute redistribution in black soil amended with 0, 0.5, and 2.0% Na 2 CO 3 . Saturated hydraulic conductivity ( K s ) was measured after 0~4 wetting-drying cycles. Soil water retention was determined by the filter paper method, and unsaturated hydraulic conductivity ( K u ) was estimated with the van Genuchten-Mualem model. A complementary column experiment applied sequential rainfall depths of 10, 20, 40, and 70 mm to track soil moisture, electrical conductivity (EC), and gravel layer water EC. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: Na 2 CO 3 addition reduced initial Kₛ from 3.31 × 10 −6 m/s at 0% to 2.49 × 10 −7 and 3.02 × 10 −8 m/s at 0.5% and 2.0%. Wetting-drying caused further declines, while estimated Kᵤ remained lower in Na 2 CO 3 -amended soils over most of the modeled suction range. During sequential rainfall, the 2.0% treatment accumulated more water near the surface and responded more slowly at depth. EC decreased in the upper 20 cm but increased at 20~40 cm, while gravel layer water EC increased by only 8.9%. Low hydraulic conductivity therefore restricted vertical water transmission and promoted solute accumulation within the soil profile.

Low hydraulic conductivity therefore restricted vertical water transmission and promoted solute accumulation within the soil profile.

papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of New Additive, 4-(3-bromophenyl)thiosemicarbazide for High-Conductivity Polymer Electrolyte
papers.abstract: Thiosemicarbazides are valued for their biological activities and versatile applications, with nitrogen and sulfur donor atoms offering new potential in polymer electrolyte studies.The main goal of this research is to synthesize and characterize 4 -(3-bromophenyl) thiosemicarbazide and investigate its conductivity.4-(3-bromophenyl)thiosemicarbazide was prepared by reacting 3-bromophenyl isothiocyanate with hydrazine hydrate and was successfully synthesized in 89% yield.CHNS analysis confirmed its high purity with <1% deviation from theoretical values.FTIR (cm⁻¹): 3275, 3146 [ν(N-H)]; 1632 [δ(NH₂) + ν(C=C)ₐᵣ]; 1571 [ν(C=C)ₐᵣ]; 1524 [δ(N-H)]; 1211 [ν(C=S)]; 1076 [ν(C-N)]; 763 [γ(C-H)ₐᵣ]; 696 [ν(C-Br)].¹³C NMR displayed signals at 180 ppm (C=S) and 121-141 ppm (aromatic carbons), confirming the proposed structure.UV-Vis spectra showed absorption at 270 and 212 nm, assigned to π→π* and n→σ* transitions, respectively.Thermogravimetric analysis revealed a multi-step decomposition, indicating its thermal stability.Single-crystal XRD revealed a monoclinic crystal system (space group P2₁/n) with unit cell parameters a = 6.2948(4)Å, α = 90°; b = 28.1751(18)Å, β = 99.168(2)°;c = 10.8098(7)Å, γ = 90°, revealing intermolecular N-H••S and N-H••Br hydrogen bonds, and C-H••π and N-H••π interactions.The UV-Vis Tauc plot gave a band gap of 5.36 eV, while DFT calculated 4.92 eV, indicating a wide-band-gap electronic structure.EIS measurements indicated an ionic conductivity of 8.87 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹ at room temperature for the sample containing 10 wt% additive.Upon incorporation of 5 wt% 2,6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid, the conductivity increased by 8.3-fold to 7.32 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ at room temperature, reaching a maximum of 8.60 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ at 50 °C, beyond which thermal degradation effects reduce conductivity.Temperature-dependent studies revealed non-Arrhenius behavior, with conductivity peaking at 50°C (8.60 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹) and declining at higher temperatures, consistent with a negative apparent activation energy (Ea = -2.21kJ/mol) arising from thermal degradation effects that dominate above 50°C.Thus, the material shows great potential as a conductive additive for polymer electrolyte-based energy storage applications, with tunable ionic transport properties within its operational temperature window (<50°C).

papers.title: Comparative Physicochemical Characterization of Green Waste Compost Tea from Different Feedstocks
papers.abstract: Rising concern over environmental impacts of excessive agrochemical fertilizer use has drove to surge in interest of converting waste into compost and compost tea, a sustainable alternative offering diverse physicochemical and biological interactions.This study characterizes the physicochemical properties of non-aerated green waste compost tea prepared from anaerobically composted green waste such as bamboo shoot (BS), banana peels (BP), green vegetables (GV) and leaves of java ginger (JG), Curcuma xanthorrhiza.Physicochemical parameters (pH, EC, TDS, ORP, salinity), nutrient concentrations (ammonium nitrogen, phosphorus), and antioxidant activity (DPPH assay) were determined alongside elemental (C, H, N, S) and FT-IR analyses.Results revealed a significant variation among feedstocks.BP consistently exhibited the most favourable composition, with significantly higher nutrient content (ammonium nitrogen 0.33 mg/L; phosphorus 11.07 mmol/L), ionic strength (EC 16.58 mS/cm; TDS 8204 mg/L), phenolic concentration, and antioxidant activity (77% inhibition).In contrast, GV and JG teas showed comparatively lower nutrient and bioactive profiles.Elemental and FT-IR analyses confirmed the presence of carbohydrates, proteins and phenolics, underscoring the chemical diversity contributed by different green wastes.Collectively, these findings demonstrate that feedstocks selection strongly influences nutrient dynamics and antioxidant potential of compost tea.This study highlights dual function of compost tea as both a nutrient source and biostimulant, supporting its application as an eco-friendly agriculture input.

papers.title: Thermal consequences of fast–charging–induced anode aging in Lithium–Ion Batteries: Lifetime, safety, and modelling
papers.abstract: Fast charging improves battery availability, but the associated lifetime loss cannot be separated from the cell's changing thermal state. This review examines the effects of operating temperature, charge rate, state of charge, and accumulated resistance on heat generation, anode evolution, and thermal safety. The discussion focuses on the interaction between persistent solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth and rate–sensitive lithium plating. As SEI–related resistance develops, irreversible heating and anode polarization increase during later charging. Plated and dead lithium add reactive material that can bring forward self–heating. Cells at comparable states of health may consequently respond differently to thermal abuse when their aging histories produce different interphases, resistance distributions, and lithium inventories. Evidence from calorimetry, abuse testing, plating diagnostics, and electrochemical–thermal models is examined to identify the internal variables that can connect lifetime prediction with safety analysis. The resulting pathway–resolved view informs charging control and thermal–safety assessment, but also shows that SEI, plating, resistance, and spatial–temperature states must be transferred consistently between service and abuse models.

The resulting pathway–resolved view informs charging control and thermal–safety assessment, but also shows that SEI, plating, resistance, and spatial–temperature states must be transferred consistently between service and abuse models.

papers.title: Antibiotic and growth factor-loaded hydrogels for infected bone defect repair: mechanisms of spatiotemporal delivery and cellular microenvironment regulation
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
papers.abstract: The treatment of infected bone defects (IBDs) requires simultaneous infection control and bone regeneration. However, traditional staged treatment protocols have several limitations. These include extended treatment durations, multiple surgical procedures, and low repair efficiency. Bifunctional hydrogels loaded with antibiotics and growth factors (GFs) offer a crucial material platform for integrated treatment strategies. These hydrogels possess excellent biocompatibility, malleability, and the capacity for spatiotemporal drug delivery. This review summarizes the design principles of antibiotic- and GF-loaded hydrogels, with particular attention to sequential and synergistic release strategies and their roles in infection control, immune regulation, vascularization, and osteogenesis. Current in vitro and in vivo evaluation approaches are also discussed, together with remaining challenges in drug stability, release precision, long-term biosafety, and clinical translation. This review may provide a basis for the rational design of multifunctional hydrogel systems and their further development for infected bone defect repair.

papers.title: Cross-domain thermal-health prediction and early warning for lithium-ion batteries via dual-stream network
papers.abstract: The joint prediction of thermal states and State of Health (SOH) is vital to ensure the safe operation and reliable management of lithium-ion batteries. However, existing approaches usually model these targets independently. Such separate modeling leads to insufficient coupling awareness, restricts practical warning decision-making, and yields poor cross-domain generalization, which impedes reliable battery lifespan management. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a dual-stream multi-task network for joint thermal-health prediction and early warning to improve battery management systems. The architecture contains two parallel branches: a temporal convolutional network captures local thermal dynamics, while a Mamba model characterizes long-range degradation evolution. The outputs of the two branches are fed into adaptive gated fusion modules followed by task-specific prediction heads. An auxiliary temperature difference prediction task is introduced to improve thermal consistency, and a weighted loss function focusing on high-temperature regions is designed to enhance prediction reliability under safety-critical conditions. A domain distribution alignment strategy is further adopted to realize few-shot cross-environment domain adaptation. After alignment-based pre-training, a small number of labeled target-domain samples are utilized for model fine-tuning. Experiments under dynamic conditions on the XJTU dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.011 for SOH and 0.898 °C for maximum temperature. Cross-environment transfer tests on the NASA dataset obtain an SOH MAE of 0.022. Relying on the prediction results, the proposed warning scheme achieves a strict timely response rate of 92.6%, with an average warning lead time of 48.6 cycles across test cases. These results verify that the proposed framework enables proactive thermal-risk monitoring and holds great application potential for intelligent battery management.

Experiments under dynamic conditions on the XJTU dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.011 for SOH and 0.898 °C for maximum temperature. These results verify that the proposed framework enables proactive thermal-risk monitoring and holds great application potential for intelligent battery management.

papers.title: Association between an improved positioning management strategy and non-incisional low back pain and sleep quality in patients undergoing modified radical mastectomy for breast cancer: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Background Non-incisional low back pain, particularly low back pain, and sleep disturbance are common yet underrecognized problems during early recovery after breast cancer surgery. This study evaluated whether an improved positioning management strategy was associated with reduced non-incisional low back pain and improved postoperative sleep quality. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult women who underwent modified radical mastectomy or simple mastectomy for breast cancer between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were grouped according to whether an improved positioning management strategy was implemented during the perioperative period (intervention vs. control). Non-incisional low back pain was assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS, 0–10), and sleep quality was assessed using the Richards–Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ: 0–100) at 24, 48, and 72 h postoperatively. Safety outcomes included total drainage volume during the first 3 postoperative days, subcutaneous seroma, and skin-flap ischemia or necrosis. Linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts were used for repeated measures, adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), analgesic regimen, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Gamma regression and Firth-penalized logistic regression were applied for safety outcomes. Results Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between groups, although BMI was slightly higher in the intervention group ( P = .04) and was adjusted for in multivariable analyses. Improved positioning management was associated with significantly lower non-incisional low back pain ( β = −0.711, P < .001). Pain increased over time in the control group, whereas significant group-by-time interactions indicated greater pain reduction in the intervention group at 48 h ( β = −0.358, P = .002) and 72 h ( β = −0.737, P < .001). Between-group differences in pain at all time points remained significant after Holm correction. The association remained significant after additional adjustment for incisional pain. Improved positioning management was also associated with higher postoperative sleep quality, with significant group and group-by-time effects at 24–72 h. No significant between-group differences were observed in drainage volume, seroma, or flap ischemia/necrosis. Conclusion An improved positioning management strategy was associated with reduced early postoperative non-incisional low back pain and better sleep quality after breast cancer surgery, without evidence of increased drainage- or flap-related complications. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations and warrant confirmation in prospective studies.

papers.title: Thermophysiological responses to occupational heat stress during simulated wildland firefighting in females and males: influence of fitness and body composition
papers.abstract: This study compared thermophysiological responses to prolonged exercise during prolonged occupational heat stress in female and male participants involved in wildland firefighting activities while wearing standard personal protective equipment. Twenty-two participants (11 females and 11 males) performed a graded exercise test followed by a prolonged submaximal protocol simulating wildfire suppression tasks in a controlled environment (30 °C, 30% relative humidity). Physiological responses, gastrointestinal temperature (T g ), chest skin temperature (T skin ), sweat production, and heat balance components were evaluated. Females exhibited higher mean values for most physiological variables, except rating of perceived exertion, which was higher in males. However, when responses were analyzed at matched relative exercise intensities, no meaningful sex-related differences were observed in T g , whereas chest T skin and heart rate remained higher in females. Body fat percentage was positively associated with T g and chest T skin ( r= 0.55 and 0.53), whereas VO 2max was negatively correlated with T g ( r= −0.47). This relationship disappeared when VO 2max was normalized to lean body mass. Heat dissipation pathways differed between groups: males showed greater evaporative heat loss, whereas females exhibited a greater contribution of dry heat exchange. These findings suggest that individual body composition and aerobic fitness may contribute to variability in thermophysiological strain during occupational uncompensable heat stress.

papers.title: Pemberdayaan Rumah Tangga Petani melalui Pengolahan Semangka Non-Grading menjadi Sirup Pasteurisasi di Kecamatan Pujut
papers.abstract: Semangka kategori *non-grading* sering kali memiliki nilai jual rendah karena tidak memenuhi standar pasar, meskipun sebenarnya masih layak dikonsumsi. Kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan pemahaman peserta mengenai pengolahan semangka *non-grading* menjadi sirop terpasteurisasi. Kegiatan dilaksanakan di Desa Segala Anyar, Kecamatan Pujut, Lombok Tengah, dengan melibatkan 15 peserta yang berasal dari keluarga petani dan Kelompok Tani Modern. Rangkaian kegiatan meliputi penyampaian materi, demonstrasi, praktik langsung, serta evaluasi melalui *pre-test* dan *post-test*. Evaluasi mencakup aspek pembuatan sirop, pasteurisasi, dan pengemasan. Skor rata-rata meningkat dari 2,55 pada *pre-test* menjadi 4,18 pada *post-test*, dengan kenaikan sebesar 1,63 poin. Peningkatan pemahaman tertinggi terjadi pada aspek pasteurisasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya peningkatan pemahaman peserta setelah pelatihan serta mengindikasikan bahwa kegiatan ini memberikan pengalaman praktis dalam mengolah semangka *non-grading* menjadi sirop terpasteurisasi.

papers.title: Epigenetic aging in the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms and implications for immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Aging reshapes the tumor microenvironment (TME) by altering the immune, stromal, and vascular compartments, yet these changes are not fully explained by chronological age. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, and non-coding RNA programs, may contribute to persistent alterations in cellular function and communication. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on epigenetic remodeling in the aged TME, distinguishing established findings in aging and cancer from mechanisms that remain to be demonstrated specifically in aged tumors. We highlight how epigenetic changes intersect with cellular senescence, chronic inflammation, and metabolic stress to weaken antitumor immunity and influence treatment response, with particular attention to T-cell dysfunction, regulatory T-cells, myeloid cells, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells. We also discuss the limitations of bulk-tissue epigenetic clocks and the emerging value of cell-resolved and spatial analyses. Finally, we consider therapeutic implications, including epigenetic therapies, senescence-directed interventions, and selective targeting of suppressive immune-stromal interactions, while noting that their ability to reverse TME aging remains uncertain. Integrating longitudinal human studies with functional experiments will be essential to determine whether epigenetically altered immune-stromal niches can serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets beyond chronological age alone.

papers.title: Sustainable Ammonium Metallates Enabling Efficient PET Waste Depolymerization
papers.abstract: Abstract The increasing volume and heterogeneity of post-consumer PET waste highlight the need for efficient and sustainable chemical recycling technologies capable of providing monomers of sufficient purity for closed-loop applications. In this work, we report a solvolytic process enabled by ammonium metallate catalysts, and in particular [TMA][FeCl4], designed to operate under less severe conditions than conventional depolymerization routes. The methodology employs methanol as the sole solvent at 170 °C, without acidic or basic additives, and affords DMT yields up to 90% at 1 mol % catalyst loading, while complete disappearance of insoluble PET is maintained even at loadings as low as 0.1 mol %. A systematic experimental plan, including catalyst screening, optimization, PET concentration effects, and mechanical-stirring assisted scale-up to 48 g of PET, demonstrates high robustness and excellent isolated yields across operating conditions. The process shows broad tolerance toward common polymeric contaminants and real post-consumer waste streams, including colored packaging and mixed textile substrates, yielding high-purity DMT after a single recrystallization. The recovered DMT was successfully reused for PET synthesis and further validated as a polyester-grade feedstock through the preparation of a PBT-based thermoplastic copolyester elastomer with properties comparable to appropriate benchmark materials. Overall, the less severe reaction conditions, low catalyst loading and cost, operational simplicity, waste-stream compatibility, and recovery of polymer-grade DMT highlight the potential of this approach for PET chemical recycling and monomer valorization.

papers.title: Environmentally Sustainable Chitin-Based Composite Structures Isolated from Lichens: Physicochemical Characterization and Biointerface Evaluation
papers.abstract: Lichens are complex symbiotic organisms composed of fungi and photosynthetic partners such as algae or cyanobacteria. While numerous bioactive compounds have been extracted from lichens, their insoluble, structural polymeric materials remain largely unexplored. In this study, the structural components of four lichen species—Xanthoparmelia pulla, Rhizoplaca chrysoleuca, Diploschistes scruposus, and Umbilicaria nylanderiana—were isolated through sequential demineralization, deproteinization, and decolorization processes to obtain sustainable biopolymeric matrices. The isolated materials were characterized using FTIR, XRD, TGA, SEM, and EDS analyses. The combined physicochemical analyses supported the presence of chitin-containing structural polysaccharides together with residual mineral components and revealed species-dependent differences in the chemical, crystalline, thermal, morphological, and elemental characteristics of the isolated materials. XRD analysis further revealed distinct diffraction profiles and contributions from residual crystalline mineral phases, particularly CaCO₃. SEM observations indicated species-dependent differences in surface morphology, while EDS confirmed the presence of C, N, O, Si, and Ca elements. The MTT assay revealed species-, concentration-, and time-dependent differences in L929 cell viability. Materials derived from X. pulla and R. chrysoleuca showed comparatively favorable cellular responses, whereas D. scruposus and U. nylanderiana caused significant reductions in cell viability. These findings provide comparative physicochemical and cellular-response data on lichen-derived structural materials and support their further investigation as naturally derived materials for potential biointerface applications.

papers.title: Double Vacancy CdS / Bi 19 Cl 3 S 27 Heterojunction with Inverted F‐Scheme and Internal Electric Field Constructed Via an Electrostatic Self‐Assembly Strategy for Boosted Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Rationally designing heterojunction photocatalysts with directional charge transfer characteristics remains a challenge. Herein, we report a novel 0D/1D dual‐vacancy CdS/Bi 19 Cl 3 S 27 (denoted as CdS v /BCS v ) heterojunction photocatalyst with an inverted F‐scheme charge transfer mechanism via electrostatic self‐assembly. This unique charge transfer mechanism enables the optimized CdS v /BCS v ‐2 heterojunction to achieve a H 2 production rate of 446.8 μmol h −1 g −1 , which is 3.6 times higher than that of pure CdS v (123.3 μmol h −1 g −1 ) and 60.4 times higher than that of pure BCS v (7.4 μmol h −1 g −1 ). Mechanistic investigations, incorporating in situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, reveal that the enhanced activity originates from the formation of the CdS v /BCS v heterojunction, which promotes efficient photoelectron transfer from CdS v to BCS v . This work proposes an inverted F‐scheme charge transfer mechanism to enhance photocatalytic activity and provides a new strategy for constructing high performance dual‐defect composite photocatalysts for photocatalytic H 2 evolution.

papers.title: Extending a Thermal Runaway Modeling Framework to Cells of Different Formats, Sizes, and Chemistries
papers.abstract: Simplified staged thermal runaway (TR) models are attractive for early-stage battery safety assessment, but they are usually parameterized for a single cell type and rely on internal temperature measurements that are impractical in sealed cylindrical and pouch cells. This work extends a four-stage TR modeling framework so it can be applied to cylindrical and pouch cells of different sizes with nickel-rich layered-oxide cathodes using surface-temperature data from accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) alone. Four modifications are introduced: an objective segmentation of the temperature-rate curve by three-segment piecewise regression with free breakpoints; a regularized extraction of the Arrhenius parameters that removes the ill-conditioned data at each stage end; a stage-dependent mass-loss function, including a two-step venting formulation for cells with delayed vent opening; and format-specific non-adiabatic boundary conditions for the severe and cooling phases. Adiabatic TR experiments were performed on three samples each of a 4.5 Ah 21700 NMC cylindrical cell, a 33 Ah 4695 NCMA cylindrical cell, and a 65 Ah NMC pouch cell. The model reproduces the measured temperature and temperature-rise rate for all three formats. The results quantify how strongly cell format governs TR severity and indicate that TR in large-format pouch cells can be accurately described without internal instrumentation. Applicability to prismatic cells and to other cathode chemistries, such as LFP, has not been demonstrated.

papers.title: A Porous Polymer of Thienothiophene and Tetraphenylethylene: Design, Synthesis and Photophysical Properties
papers.abstract: A novel conjugated porous polymer (CPP) based on thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT) and tetraphenylethylene (TPE) was successfully designed and synthesized via a Pd(0)-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling reaction. Owing to its rigid, highly cross-linked architecture, the resulting TT–TPE polymer is insoluble and exhibits permanent porosity. Comprehensive characterization using UV–Vis, fluorescence, and FTIR spectroscopy, together with scanning electron microscopy (SEM), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), confirmed the successful formation of a robust π-conjugated porous network. The polymer exhibits a strong π–π* absorption band at 392 nm, intense fluorescence emission at 549 nm, and a large Stokes shift, indicating efficient intramolecular energy transfer and significant excited-state relaxation. SEM images reveal a hierarchically porous, sponge-like morphology, while electrochemical studies demonstrate stable redox behavior and favorable HOMO and LUMO energy levels, highlighting its potential for optoelectronic applications. Furthermore, the optical and electrochemical band gaps are in good agreement, indicating the reliability of the experimental results. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further corroborate the experimental findings, showing excellent agreement between the simulated and observed electronic transitions. Overall, the TT–TPE conjugated porous polymer represents a promising functional material for applications in chemical sensing, energy storage, and optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Structure–property relationships in SPEEK-PVDF blend membranes: balancing proton conductivity and hydrothermal stability
papers.journal: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract Sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) (SPEEK) and poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) blend membranes were prepared to investigate the balance between hydrothermal stability and proton conductivity for their potential application as proton exchange membrane (PEM). The degree of sulfonation of SPEEK was found to be 66% (IEC=1.99 ± 0.02 meq/g), attained by using a controlled sulfonation procedure. SPEEK was blended with low molecular weight PVDF (71,000 g/mol) in different proportions. The membranes were prepared by solution casting and post-casting temperature’s influence was analysed on the structure morphology and performance of the membrane. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) displayed a common three-stage degradation profile, which corresponds to the release of moisture, the breaking down of sulfonic groups and the decomposition of the polymer backbone. Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) revealed that the miscibility of SPEEK and PVDF is highly dependent on the temperature of solvent evaporation, which affects the formation of hydrophilic and hydrophobic structures. The homogenization of the membranes was evaluated through elemental analysis from Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS). In sorption-desorption experiments, it was seen that there are two stages of absorption that are controlled by hydration of sulfonic sites and capillary absorption. It was determined that increased post-casting temperatures result in less absorption and swelling. The proton conductivity and hydrothermal stability showed an inverse relationship with the membranes cast at 60-70 °C. The present study demonstrates that the conditions under which membranes are made affect the performance of the blend membranes.

papers.title: Pyro‐Phototronic Effect in Two‐Dimensional Graphene/AgCrP 2 S 6 /Graphene Heterojunction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The pyro‐phototronic effect has been identified as a promising strategy for improving the performance of photodetectors. In this study, we report the discovery of the pyro‐phototronic effect in the graphene/AgCrP 2 S 6 /graphene (Gr/AgCrP 2 S 6 /Gr) heterojunction. Multilayer AgCrP 2 S 6 exhibits a non‐centrosymmetric structure induced by interlayer sliding, as experimentally verified by second‐harmonic generation (SHG) and piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM). Furthermore, the fabricated Gr/AgCrP 2 S 6 /Gr heterojunction, which exhibits a peak pyroelectric coefficient of 9638 µC·m −2 ·K −1 . The pyro‐phototronic effect of the heterojunction is systematically investigated under varying wavelengths, optical power intensities, bias voltages, and modulation frequencies. The pyro‐phototronic effect markedly enhances the heterojunction's output current density, achieving a remarkable 14.57‐fold increase relative to the performance based solely on the photovoltaic effect. Specifically, under 405 nm illumination, the heterojunction achieves peak photodetection metrics: responsivity of 46.01 mA/W, external quantum efficiency of 14.09%, and specific detectivity of 2.2 × 10 11 Jones. These findings deepen the understanding of multi‐field coupling mechanisms in 2D materials and establish a new paradigm for the design and development of high‐performance photodetectors leveraging the pyro‐phototronic effect.

papers.title: Case Report: An Overview of Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis in A 2-Year-Old Child Clinical Symptoms and Nutritional Therapy
papers.abstract: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) is a severe mucocutaneous reaction characterized by extensive necrosis and detachment of the epidermis, which can lead to metabolic disturbances and increased nutritional requirements. Its management necessitates a comprehensive approach, including nutritional support. This report describes the clinical manifestations and nutritional management of a pediatric patient with Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis. It is a descriptive case report based on data from the patient's medical history, physical examination, laboratory findings, diagnosis, treatment, and the monitoring of clinical status and nutritional condition throughout the course of care. The data were analyzed descriptively by comparing the patient's status over the treatment period. The findings indicate that a 2-year-old girl developed a red rash, blisters, and skin peeling following the administration of Novagesik. Examinations revealed epidermolysis covering approximately 89% of the body surface area, a positive Nikolsky sign, and involvement of the ocular, oral (lip), and genital mucosa. The patient presented with malnutrition, leukopenia, hyponatremia, and hypoalbuminemia. Management included fluid therapy, antibiotics, corticosteroids, wound care, and enteral nutritional therapy via a nasogastric tube, utilizing a high-calorie, high-protein formula. Throughout the treatment, there was an improvement in clinical condition and laboratory parameters, as well as an increase in body weight. Recognizing the characteristic clinical manifestations supports a diagnosis of Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis, while enteral nutritional therapy serves as a crucial component of supportive care, helping to meet energy and protein requirements during the recovery process.

papers.title: Experimental Study on the Inhibition of Hydrogen/Methane/Air Explosion by Potassium Oxalate Water Mist
papers.abstract: Abstract The suppression characteristics of hydrogen/methane/air explosion by water mist with potassium oxalate (K2C2O4·H2O) additive were experimentally investigated in this work. The effects of pure water mist and K2C2O4·H2O-modified water mist on flame morphology, average flame propagation speed, maximum flame acceleration, explosion pressure, and maximum pressure rise rate were systematically analyzed. Results indicated that the inhibition efficiency of pure water mist is limited and reaches saturation with increasing concentration, while the addition of K2C2O4·H2O significantly enhances the explosion suppression performance. With the increase of K2C2O4·H2O mass fraction, the average flame propagation speed and maximum flame acceleration are gradually reduced, the peak explosion pressure and maximum pressure rise rate are observably decreased, and the time to reach peak pressure is obviously delayed. When the mass fraction of K2C2O4·H2O is above 6%, the pressure evolution curve is transformed from a three-stage mode to a four-stage mode. Based on TG-DSC experimental analysis, the thermal decomposition process of K2C2O4·H2O is determined as dehydration and decomposition to produce K2CO3 and CO. The physical–chemical synergistic explosion suppression mechanism is revealed, in which physical effects including endothermic cooling, inert dilution, and flame destruction provide favorable conditions for chemical inhibition, and chemical chain termination reduces heat release and strengthens physical suppression. The findings can provide theoretical support for the safety protection of hydrogen/methane/air systems.

papers.title: The effects of physical exercise on executive function, internalizing symptoms and externalizing symptoms in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background The aim of this study is to comprehensively assess the potential effects of physical exercise on executive function, internalizing symptoms and externalizing symptoms in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and to explore the moderating factors influencing these effects. Methods We performed a systematic search of six databases (including Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, PsycNET, the Cochrane Library and SPORTDiscus). Data analysis was performed using R software, and a meta-analysis was conducted using a random-effects model to estimate the pooled effect size. In addition, subgroup analyses and meta-regression were conducted to explore potential moderating factors. Results A total of 25 randomised controlled trials involving 1,116 participants were included. With low certainty of evidence, the pooled effect of inhibitory control was statistically significant ( g = 0.45, p < 0.01). With very low certainty of evidence, the pooled effect of internalizing symptoms was statistically significant ( g = 0.97, p = 0.03). The pooled effects of cognitive flexibility ( g = 0.69, p = 0.054), working memory ( g = 0.28, p = 0.10), and externalizing symptoms ( g = 0.64, p = 0.29) did not reach statistical significance, all rated as very low certainty of evidence. Conclusion Physical exercise may be positively associated with inhibitory control in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, the effects of interventions show high heterogeneity, have wide confidence intervals, and exhibit limited stability. Systematic review registration PROSPERO CRD420261380631.

papers.title: Constructing Thermoreversible Diels–Alder Networks in SBS Elastomers via a Green Fabrication Strategy
papers.abstract: A thermoreversible cross-linked styrene–butadiene–styrene (SBS) based on Diels–Alder (DA) chemistry was fabricated via a solvent-free melt processing approach. Maleated SBS was adopted so that furfurylamine could be grafted onto pendant anhydride groups to introduce furan moieties. Functionalized SBS was then cross-linked with bismaleimide through DA coupling. Thermoreversibility and network dynamics of the DA-crosslinked SBS (DSBS) were characterized by FTIR spectroscopy, solubility assessment, DSC analysis, and tensile testing. FTIR spectroscopy results verified the successful furfurylamine grafting and DA cross-linking mediated by bismaleimide in the DSBS. The DSBS exhibited enhanced solvent resistance, thermal stability and mechanical performance. The Diels–Alder (DA) linkages within the DSBS network undergo thermally induced dissociation at elevated temperatures (>140 °C) and readily reform at 110 °C, thereby enabling reversible and repeatable network reconstruction. Furthermore, the mechanical properties of DSBS can be systematically tailored by varying the bismaleimide content. Specifically, increasing the bismaleimide concentration results in enhanced ultimate tensile strength and elastic modulus, accompanied by a reduction in ductility. These findings demonstrate an efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally sustainable approach for the fabrication of high-performance, recyclable SBS elastomers.
papers.summary: A thermoreversible cross-linked styrene–butadiene–styrene (SBS) based on Diels–Alder (DA) chemistry was fabricated via a solvent-free melt processing approach. The DSBS exhibited enhanced solvent resistance, thermal stability and mechanical performance. These findings demonstrate an efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally sustainable approach for the fabrication of high-performance, recyclable SBS elastomers.

papers.title: Upcycling Secondary Cellulosic Fibres and Post-Industrial Recycled Polypropylene from Household Appliance Manufacturing into Circular Composites with Enhanced Dimensional Stability
papers.abstract: This study addresses the development, thermal characterisation, and dimensional stability of circular composites based on a post-industrial recycled polypropylene (rPP) matrix from household appliances. The matrix was reinforced with natural (B600 and BC300) and recycled (SIS250, PWC500, and ZZC500) cellulosic fibres at 10%, 20%, and 30% dosages, using 3% MAPP as a compatibilizer. Processing was conducted via twin-screw extrusion and injection moulding. Systematic evaluations (TGA-DTG, DSC, and DIL) showed a minor reduction (2.6–5.1%) in thermal degradation onset, maintaining a safe processing window. Cellulosic fibres generally promoted matrix crystallization through heterogeneous nucleation, increasing matrix crystallinity up to 39.3% in composite B600-30 compared to 20.4% for the reference rPP matrix. Furthermore, the reinforcements acted as dimensional stabilizers, reducing the linear thermal expansion coefficient (α40−120) by up to 28.9% (ZZC500-30) while increasing thermal conductivity by up to 32.7% (B600 series). This approach demonstrates a viable upcycling strategy, yielding high-secondary-content circular composites by combining post-industrial recycled polypropylene matrices with reinforcements (virgin wood cellulose benchmarks (B600 and BC300), pre-consumer recycled cellulose (PWC500), post-consumer recycled cellulose (ZZC500), and recycled technical sisal (SIS250), complemented by 3 wt.% commercial MAPP compatibilizer.

papers.title: Adaptive Ferroic Bi‐Sb Hybrid Iodides for Multi‐Modal Energy Harvesting and Phototronics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI 5 (HBI) and HDASbI 5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi 0.5 Sb 0.5 I 5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1 H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in pancreatic cancer surgery: evidence maturity, boundaries, and clinical translation
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer surgery requires decisions about resectability, treatment sequencing, operative planning, complications, and prognosis. We mapped artificial intelligence (AI) studies to five surgical decision domains and evaluated study design, validation, performance, decision utility, workflow fit, and evidence limitations. This structured narrative review included 31 direct AI studies and three adjacent or protocol studies; only direct AI studies underwent evidence-maturity grading. Eighteen studies met Level 1, ten Level 2, and three Level 3; none reached Levels 4 or 5. Three-dimensional assessment of vascular involvement has undergone external and prospective performance validation, but its effect on surgical decisions or patient outcomes remains unproven. Automated segmentation can aid anatomical visualization, although tumor delineation and workflow demands limit use. Transcriptomic analyses of trial samples suggest differential adjuvant treatment benefit but do not establish prospective biomarker-guided treatment allocation. Models for complications, recurrence, and survival offer risk-stratification signals, yet calibration, actionable thresholds, class imbalance, and clinical utility remain concerns. AI should support radiologists, surgeons, and multidisciplinary teams rather than replace their judgment. Clinical adoption requires robust external validation, prospective workflow assessment, and evidence that AI-assisted decisions improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Al1−xHfxN Thin Films with Enhanced Piezoelectric Responses for GHz Surface Acoustic Wave Devices
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Ternary compounds obtained by alloying wurtzite AlN with transition metals have emerged as promising materials with significantly enhanced piezoelectric characteristics relative to binary AlN. The increased electromechanical coupling in these compounds boosts the performance of high‐frequency acoustic devices. To date, progress has largely focused on aluminum scandium nitride (), which, while widely deployed, relies on scandium, a costly and critical element that is challenging to refine. Here, we investigate aluminum hafnium nitride () as a more economical and accessible alternative to . Using reactive co‐sputtering on both Si and ‐ substrates, we demonstrate wurtzite thin films () with strong ‐axis texture and nearly isotropic lattice expansion upon Hf incorporation. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy indicates cross‐gap hybridization between N 2 and Hf 5 states, which can enhance the Born effective charge and, thereby, the piezoelectric response. The incorporation of Hf leads to a multifold enhancement in the piezoelectric coefficient, , relative to AlN, despite increasing structural disorder in these thin films. Building on this increased electromechanical coupling, we present functional GHz surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators that exhibit enhanced performance, as well as efficient excitation of bulk acoustic waves with low propagation losses. These results establish as a promising platform for next‐generation high‐frequency electromechanical devices, with prospects for further piezoelectric enhancements through improved epitaxy.

papers.title: Dataset merging strategy for efficient construction of a machine-learning force field: A case of CeO2 surfaces with an oxygen vacancy
papers.abstract: The accuracy and transferability of machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) critically depend on the quality of the training database. Here, we propose a dataset merging strategy for efficiently constructing a transferable MLFF for pristine and oxygen-defective CeO2 surfaces. The proposed strategy is based on three key elements: (1) initiating on-the-fly training from small, less stable slab models to accelerate early stage convergence by sampling diverse high-energy configurations; (2) sampling diverse local structures by gradually increasing the temperature during molecular dynamics simulations while avoiding excessively rapid atomic motions and unphysically short contacts; and (3) merging independently generated datasets from slab models with different thicknesses and defect conditions to improve transferability. The resulting MLFF is validated on larger slab models containing 144 atoms and applied to structural optimization of pristine and oxygen-defective surfaces as well as lattice oxygen diffusion pathways on defective surfaces. The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. Furthermore, the merged MLFF was applied to ideal CeO2(111) slabs containing up to 5183 atoms, yielding only weak size dependence of the predicted vacancy-migration barrier. These results highlight that systematic dataset merging across model sizes and configurations provides a practical route to constructing transferable MLFFs for complex oxide surfaces.

The predicted pathways and energy barriers are in good agreement with density functional theory results, particularly for pathways involving relatively large structural and energetic changes. papers.title: Promise and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation: a feasibility study
papers.abstract: PurposeTo evaluate the feasibility and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation and deep learning-based segmentation.ApproachWe developed ChameleonNet, a framework utilizing the Contrastive Unpaired Translation (CUT) network with decoupled contrastive learning (DCL) loss to synthesize noncontrast CT from contrast CT scans. Using annotations of four heart chambers (left atrium (LA), left ventricle (LV), right atrium (RA), and right ventricle (RV)) from contrast scans, we trained a Hausdorff distance loss-enhanced nnU-Net on synthesized noncontrast images. The translation model was trained with 35,538 contrast-enhanced and 37,197 noncontrast CT slices. The segmentation model was trained with 292 synthesized noncontrast scans. Performance was evaluated using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 95th Hausdorff distance (HD95) on 36 synthesized noncontrast scans, and volume agreement on 36 real noncontrast CT scans was assessed using Pearson correlation, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and mean percentage error (MPE).ResultsThe segmentation model achieved DSC of 0.94 (±0.01), 0.91 (±0.04), 0.92 (±0.03), 0.93 (±0.02), and HD95 of 3.63 (±1.49), 5.74 (±4.08), 5.18 (±1.77), and 5.51 (±3.21) mm on synthesized noncontrast images for LA, LV, RA, and RV, respectively. On real noncontrast CT scans, Pearson correlations were 0.93, 0.82, 0.87, and 0.89 (all p<0.001), with MAPE ranging from 9.22% to 20.79%, and MPE ranging from −12.52% to 4.67%.ConclusionsChameleonNet demonstrated feasibility for heart chamber segmentation from noncontrast CT without manual noncontrast annotations. However, volume errors, particularly for LV and RV, indicate that further refinement and validation are needed before clinical use.

papers.title: Supramolecular Binary Systems of Flavonoids: Design, Structure, and Physicochemical Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, an environmentally friendly mechanochemical approach was used to prepare and characterize a series of new cocrystals and salt cocrystals with a 1:2 stoichiometry. The flavonoids apigenin (APG), luteolin (LUT), fisetin (FIS), kaempferol (KAE), and quercetin (QUE) were mixed with pyridarone [4-(1-benzofuran-2-yl)pyridine (BZFP)] as the coformer. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), combined with Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) and Fourier transform Raman (FT-Raman) spectroscopy, confirmed the formation of well-defined supramolecular architectures stabilized predominantly by intermolecular O−H···N bonds. These interactions involve the terminal hydroxyl groups of the flavonoids (7OH and 3′OH/4′OH) acting as hydrogen bond donors and the pyridyl nitrogen atoms of BZFP serving as acceptors. The nature and dynamics of the hydrogen bonding network were further investigated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Analysis of the N 1s spectra revealed proton transfer in the LUT/BZFP, KAE/BZFP, and QUE/BZFP binary systems, indicating the presence of a mixed neutral−salt character. The remaining cocrystals were neutral. Thermal analysis showed that the obtained cocrystals have greater thermal stability than the pure components. Dissolution kinetics, solubility, and octanol−water partition coefficient studies (using chromatographic methods)compared to the parent flavonoidsrevealed a significant increase in dissolution rates, saturation concentrations, and solubility of the neutral and salt cocrystals under simulated gastric conditions (pH 1.9). Dissolution rates, saturation concentrations, and solubility values change with acidity in a complex manner. These variations can be explained by two opposing effects: on one hand, increased acidity protonates BZFP, making both pure BZFP and the cocrystals highly soluble, while the flavonoids become neutral and only sparingly soluble. Conversely, when acidity decreases, BZFP becomes neutral, reducing its solubility but increasing that of the flavonoids due to ionization. Overall, these results demonstrate that mechanochemical synthesis is a practical, effective, and sustainable strategy for improving the physicochemical properties of potent bioactive natural compounds, which can possibly be used in pharmaceutical formulations.

papers.title: Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

papers.title: Multi-Electron Transfer in Zinc-Based Batteries: Unraveling Redox Mechanisms Toward Next-Generation Self-Powered Technologies
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of autonomous IoT networks and wearable electronics has intensified the demand for photo-rechargeable zinc-based batteries (PRZBBs). While realizing high overall energy conversion efficiency intrinsically relies on cathode materials capable of multi-electron transfer reactions, current literature largely treats the fundamental electrochemistry of aqueous zinc batteries and the macroscopic engineering of solar-integrated devices as isolated domains. This review bridges this critical gap, offering a unique positioning by establishing a unified analytical framework that directly links fundamental multi-electron redox mechanisms to the dynamic architectural requirements of PRZBBs. Moving beyond a conventional cataloging of material classes, we critically evaluate diverse cathode platforms, including transition metal oxides, Prussian blue analogues, organics, halogens, and sulfur. Our incremental contribution lies in decoupling how specific multi-step reaction kinetics, distinct voltage plateaus, and dominant charge carriers dictate solar cell coupling strategies, particularly concerning maximum power point matching and intermittent charging adaptability. Furthermore, we critically and systematically assess the practical bottlenecks of these chemistries, such as shuttle effects, kinetic limitations, and voltage hysteresis, that hinder scalable integration. Finally, we distill these insights into a prioritized, roadmap-oriented perspective, outlining the short- to long-term engineering and scientific milestones necessary to translate fundamental multi-electron zinc chemistry into next-generation, commercially viable self-powered technologies.

papers.title: High-precision characterization of scattering losses in YAG and Yb:YAG ceramics with an integrating sphere and multipass-cell
papers.abstract: Abstract Transparent ceramic laser materials have been extensively studied for high-power laser applications, where scattering loss is a significant factor affecting laser output power. This study presents a method based on an integrating sphere combined with a multipass cell for measuring the scattering and absorption coefficients of laser materials, providing improved measurement precision. Pure YAG and Yb:YAG ceramic samples were investigated and systematically compared with pure YAG and Yb:YAG single crystals with the same Yb 3+ doping concentration. Specifically, the scattering coefficients at 1064 nm were measured to be 0.0046 cm −1 for YAG ceramic and 0.0093 cm −1 for Yb:YAG ceramic, while the corresponding absorption coefficients were 0.0267 cm −1 and 0.0221 cm −1 , respectively, which are close to those of the single crystals. Furthermore, overall optical quality and wavefront distortion were analyzed using a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor. The proposed method increases the effective optical interaction length, enhances the detectable loss signal, and improves measurement reliability, providing a practical approach for characterizing scattering and absorption losses in low-loss laser materials.

papers.title: Cavity-Filling Calcite in the Deccan Traps as a Natural Analogue for Mineral Carbon Sequestration and Low-Temperature Deformation
papers.abstract: Cavity-filling calcite is among the most widespread secondary phases in the Deccan Traps, and its position late in the amygdale paragenesis, after zeolites and silica phases, is long established. Two questions that remain open are addressed here: whether this calcite retains a mechanical record of deformation imposed after the cavities were sealed, and what a naturally carbonated flood-basalt pile can tell us about the durability of engineered mineral carbon storage. Calcite from three closely spaced amygdaloidal basalt exposures in the district of Maharashtra, Ane Ghat in Junnar taluka, Pune, Shindewadi 1 and Shindewadi 2 in Parner taluka, Ahilyanagar was examined by transmitted-light petrography, scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (SEM–EDS) and micro-Raman spectroscopy, with growth features deliberately separated from post-growth strain features. All three occurrences comprise coarse, optically continuous calcite grown into open voids: rhombohedral cleavage is perfect, birefringence is extreme, planar crystal faces survive in secondary-electron images, and no replacement front is developed against the basalt wall. Superimposed on this growth fabric are closely spaced polysynthetic e-twin lamellae, undulose extinction, cleavage-controlled intracrystalline microfractures, and healed fractures carrying trails of secondary inclusions. Because these features truncate cleavage and crystal boundaries that are continuous elsewhere in the same individual, they post-date crystal growth. Twin morphology is dominated by thin, straight lamellae, which on the Ferrill classification indicates deformation below roughly 170–200 ◦C. EDS spectra confirm a Cacarbonate composition; because light-element quantification in a coated carbonate is not reliable, measured Ca/C atomic ratios of 1.31–1.61 depart substantially from the ideal value of unity and the analyses are treated as semi-quantitative throughout. Micro-Raman spectra are those of well-ordered calcite, with lattice modes near 156 and 279–281 cm−1 and internal modes at 711–712 cm−1 (ν4) and 1085–1087 cm−1 (ν1); differences between sites do not exceed instrument calibration uncertainty. The results are placed in the framework of in situ mineral carbon sequestration. Deccan amygdale calcite is a completed natural experiment in basalt carbonation: divalent cations liberated by fluid–rock interaction was fixed as a thermodynamically stable carbonate that has survived approximately 66 million years in the same pore volume now targeted for engineered CO2 injection. The microstructural record modifies that otherwise reassuring picture in a specific way. Mineralized amygdales were subsequently strained, brittle microfractures propagated through the carbonate cement, and those fractures were later healed by carbonate-bearing fluids. Permanence of mineral trapping in a tectonically quiescent plateau interior is therefore neither unconditional nor catastrophically compromised: it is a balance between fracture generation and carbonate self-sealing that can be read directly from the cement.
papers.summary: Cavity-filling calcite is among the most widespread secondary phases in the Deccan Traps, and its position late in the amygdale paragenesis, after zeolites and silica phases, is long established. Twin morphology is dominated by thin, straight lamellae, which on the Ferrill classification indicates deformation below roughly 170–200 ◦C. The results are placed in the framework of in situ mineral carbon sequestration.

papers.title: Cross-stress transcriptomic integration in Marchantia polymorpha reveals stress-specific expression of regulated cell-death-associated genes
papers.abstract: Regulated cell death (RCD) contributes to plant development, stress adaptation, and immunity, but whether RCD-associated genes show conserved transcriptional responses across diverse stresses remains unclear. Here, we performed a comparative reanalysis of publicly available Marchantia polymorpha RNA-seq datasets to investigate recurrent and stress-specific expression of RCD-associated genes. We uniformly processed 36 RNA-seq samples from three independent studies, yielding nine stress-versus-control comparisons: eight abiotic (seven from one study and an independent high-light experiment) and one pathogen infection. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified for each of the 9 stress datasets compared to their respective controls, which were then examined for shared DEGs among different sets of stress vs. control comparisons. A curated list of 14 RCD-associated genes previously identified in M. polymorpha were used to examine conservation of transcriptional response. Integrated expression data were additionally examined using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) after batch correction of dataset. Of 34 DEGs shared across all nine comparisons, only 12 changed in the same direction in every comparison. The 34 genes included two transcription factors, an AP2/ERF-family factor (Mp5g22160) and a bHLH factor (Mp2g00890), which were upregulated in infection and Schröder high-light but downregulated in all seven Tan et al. comparisons. Among 14 curated RCD-associated genes, 10 were differentially expressed in at least one comparison, and MpZOU2 was the only one regulated in more than one (upregulated in cold, darkness and infection; downregulated in Tan high-light). WGCNA identified 64 co-expression modules, including an infection-associated module enriched in protein ubiquitination, proteasome-mediated degradation, ER-associated degradation, autophagy, and membrane trafficking, and a nitrogen-deficiency and osmotic-stress-associated module enriched in oxidative stress responses and cell-wall organization. Together, these findings indicate that M. polymorpha does not exhibit a uniform transcriptional RCD program across diverse stresses. Instead, RCD-associated genes appear to be selectively recruited within broader, context-dependent stress-response networks. The recurrent regulation of MpZOU2 identifies it as a candidate for functional investigation, while emphasizing that transcript-level changes alone do not establish RCD execution.

papers.title: One-step microbial conversion of waste molasses into bioactive fulvic-like acid fertilizer for sustainable soil quality improvement and agricultural waste valorization
papers.abstract: Waste molasses (WM), a carbon rich by-product of sugar production, is frequently underutilized, resulting in environmental pollution and resource loss. In this study, a one-step microbial bioconversion process using Bacillus subtilis was developed to transform WM into molasses derived fulvic acid (MFA). The highest MFA yield (33.54%) was achieved at 35 °C, 48 h, and a 5% inoculation rate. Integrated GC-MS and LC-MS analyses revealed dynamic substrate transformation during fermentation and suggested that 4-hydroxy-2-methylacetophenone, 4-oxododecanedioic acid, and 3-hydroxy-2-octylpentanedioic acid were putative intermediates involved in MFA formation. Structural characterization showed that the resulting MFA possessed a loose, porous morphology and abundant hydroxyl, carboxyl, and carbonyl groups. In a single 150 d field trial, MFA application was associated with higher soil organic carbon and humus contents than the unfertilized control and promoted maize vegetative growth. MFA also enriched the microbial communities including Pseudomonas , Acidobacterium , Actinobacteria , and Bacteroidetes . The abundance of several genes related to carbon assimilation and carboxylation, including rbcL , rbcS , accB , accC , and pccA , has also increased. Metabolomic analysis further revealed shifts in metabolites associated with central carbon metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway MFA application also markedly promoted maize growth without chemical fertilizer input, demonstrating its potential as an organic soil amendment and partial fertilizer substitute. Collectively, these findings suggest that a one-step microbial transformation can convert WM into functional fulvic-like acid fertilizer. This method provides a potential route for mineral derived FA production. Simultaneously combining the reuse of agricultural waste, improvement of soil quality, reduction of partial fertilizer dependence, and development of circular agriculture.

papers.title: N-Doped Carbon-Confined Metal Sulfide Heterojunctions for Solar Water Evaporation and Adsorption-Assisted Photocatalytic Antibiotic Removal
papers.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers a promising route for freshwater production, yet organic micropollutants such as tetracycline (TC) in feedwater may become enriched during evaporation, jeopardizing water quality. Herein, we design a dual-functional Co8FeS8/Co9S8-based aerogel (denoted as CFS/CS@NC-H) via H2/Ar etching, which simultaneously achieves high-rate evaporation and in situ TC degradation. The introduced sulfur vacancies and the bimetallic sulfide heterostructure broaden light absorption, suppress radiative electron–hole recombination, and promote nonradiative relaxation, giving rise to a synergistic photothermal–photocatalytic effect. Raman spectroscopy and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analyses further reveal that the Co8FeS8/Co9S8-based material effectively activates water molecules and substantially reduces the evaporation enthalpy. Consequently, under 1 sun illumination, the CFS/CS@NC-H aerogel delivers an evaporation rate of 2.31 kg m–2h–1 in pure water, and comparable rates are sustained in lake water, seawater, heavy metal-containing wastewater, and TC solution, demonstrating excellent salt resistance and practical adaptability. During evaporation, the aerogel efficiently degrades TC, thereby mitigating the risk of pollutant accumulation. The detoxification efficacy was further validated via pea sprout germination bioassays; the degraded TC solution achieved a germination rate of 84%, closely approaching that of pure water (90%) and far surpassing that of the untreated TC solution (56%), unequivocally confirming the drastic reduction in biological toxicity resulting from the catalytic degradation. This work highlights H2/Ar etching as an effective strategy to engineer transition metal sulfide-based materials for integrated solar evaporation and pollutant degradation, holding significant promise for sustainable water purification in complex aquatic environments.
