papers.title: Carbon Pore Architecture for Sulfur Accommodation, Retention, and Electrochemical Kinetics in Lithium–Sulfur Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Lithium–sulfur cells provide an ideal platform for studying how carbon pore architecture governs sulfur accommodation, polysulfide retention, and electrochemical kinetics. Although porous carbons with different pore characteristics have been investigated, their intrinsic pore-structure effects remain difficult to distinguish because previous studies generally employ independently synthesized carbons with different surface chemistries and morphologies. Here, we establish an experimental platform by systematically blending commercial porous carbons with controlled pore architectures while preserving their intrinsic physicochemical properties. Dynamic image analysis, gas adsorption, electron microscopy, elemental mapping, and thermogravimetric analysis reveal systematic changes in pore structure, particle morphology, sulfur distribution, and sulfur retention as the carbon ratio is varied. Sulfur confined within micropore-dominated structures exhibits greater thermal stability than sulfur accommodated in mesopore-dominated structures, demonstrating that sulfur accommodation and sulfur retention are fundamentally different processes. Electrochemical measurements further establish a clear structure–property relationship, showing that micropore-dominated architectures enhance sulfur retention but impede ion transport, whereas mesopore-dominated architectures facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of sulfur confinement and electrode stability. An optimized pore architecture balances these competing effects, enabling efficient sulfur utilization, suppressed polysulfide migration, improved reaction kinetics, and stable cycling under high sulfur loading. As a result, this study provides mechanistic insight and practical design principles for rational pore-architecture engineering in lithium–sulfur cells.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Synthesis Characterization and Thermal Properties of Homomer and Copolymers of N-Benzylmaleimide
papers.journal: American Journal of Polymer Science and Technology
papers.abstract: N-Benzylmaleimide (NBMI) was synthesized and subsequently copolymerized with methyl methacrylate (MMA) through free-radical polymerization in tetrahydrofuran (THF), using azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN) and benzoyl peroxide (BPO) as initiators. The synthesized NBMI homopolymer and NBMI-MMA copolymer (CBMI) were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR) spectroscopy, solubility studies, intrinsic-viscosity measurements, gel permeation chromatography (GPC), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The NBMI homopolymer and CBMI copolymer were obtained in yields of 39.5% and 44.0%, respectively, with intrinsic-viscosity values of 0.031 and 0.060 dL/g. FT-IR and 1 H NMR analyses confirmed the consumption of the maleimide carbon–carbon double bond during polymerization, while the characteristic imide-ring structure remained intact. Solubility studies revealed that the CBMI copolymer exhibited favourable solubility in several organic solvents. GPC analysis showed that the copolymer possessed a molecular weight of 25,881 g mol −1 . Furthermore, TGA demonstrated a predominantly single-stage degradation pattern and satisfactory thermal stability. The higher yield and intrinsic viscosity of CBMI compared with the NBMI homopolymer indicate the successful incorporation of MMA into the polymer system. Overall, the results demonstrate that NBMI-MMA copolymer exhibits favourable structural, physicochemical, and thermal characteristics, making it a promising material for potential advanced polymer applications.

papers.title: Recent advances in critical care nutrition: from dose escalation to phase-guided and response-guided care
papers.abstract: Purpose of review To critically appraise recent advances that are shifting critical care nutrition from uniform nutrient targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided care, with particular emphasis on major studies published in 2025–2026. Recent findings Recent large trials do not support routine early full-dose energy or high-dose protein delivery in unselected critically ill patients, and some higher dose strategies have generated safety signals. Indirect calorimetry improves measurement of energy expenditure, but measured expenditure is not synonymous with the dose that should be delivered. Emerging data suggest that dynamic responses, including early phosphate trajectories, may help identify metabolic readiness for feeding, although no validated bedside marker exists. Pharmacological intravenous vitamin C has shown no benefit and recurring harm signals in shocked patients, whereas micronutrient care should distinguish physiological requirements and deficiency correction from megadosing. After ICU discharge, intake frequently falls during the transition from enteral to oral nutrition, and intake-guided protocols have achieved high nutritional adequacy in proof-of-concept studies. Summary Critical care nutrition is moving from universal targets towards phase-guided, phenotype-guided and response-guided treatment. Acute-phase caution should not become prolonged underfeeding; repeated metabolic assessment, body composition, reliable intake monitoring and continuity through recovery are central priorities.

papers.title: RSM-based optimization of mechanical and moisture resistance properties of ternary polymer nanocomposites
papers.abstract: Abstract Epoxy-based polymer Nanocomposites are widely investigated for electrical insulation applications due to their exceptional mechanical and dielectric properties; however, moisture absorption and brittleness remain major challenges. This study aimed to develop and optimize Epoxy/ Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) /nano-silica ternary nanocomposites with increased tensile strength and reduced water absorption using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on Central Composite Design (CCD). The effects of EPDM concentration, nano-silica loading, and sonication time were evaluated through 20 experimental runs. Water absorption was measured according to ASTM D570 after 240-hour immersion, while tensile strength was determined using ASTM D638 standard. The statistical analysis showed that all three processing parameters significantly affected the measured responses within the investigated experimental ranges, with nano-silica loading showing the largest statistical effect. The developed linear models showed satisfactory fit and predictive statistics, with non-significant lack-of-fit results. Increasing nano-silica loading and sonication time was associated with increased tensile strength and reduced water absorption within the experimental design space. These response trends may be related to changes in the polymer–filler environment and the processing-dependent state of the silica-containing phase. The optimized formulation exhibited a tensile strength of 90.9 ± 0.46 MPa and water absorption of 0.0441 ± 0.0003% under the investigated test conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of the Epoxy/EPDM/nano-silica system as a candidate for further investigation in electrical-insulation applications.

papers.title: Forest-residue-derived constituents for low-carbon cementitious materials: evidence boundaries, quantitative trade-offs, and cold-region service qualification
papers.abstract: Forest-residue-derived constituents are increasingly being considered for low-carbon cementitious materials, but their functions differ substantially and should not be treated as a single waste-substitution category. Wood ash may serve as a screened supplementary cementitious material or mineral filler, wood-derived biochar mainly modifies hydration and pore-water behavior at low dosage, and wood fiber acts primarily as crack-control reinforcement. This review compares these three material classes through their source-specific characteristics, quantitative performance ranges, and governing microstructural mechanisms. Direct evidence from wood-derived constituents is distinguished from mechanistic analog evidence from non-wood biomass ashes and lignocellulosic fibers. Published studies commonly examine wood ash at approximately 5%–20% cement replacement and biochar at low dosages, often at approximately 0.5–3 wt% of binder, while wood and related lignocellulosic fibers are generally used at low volume fractions. These ranges are screening values rather than universal design limits because performance depends strongly on processing, water demand, dispersion, interfacial behavior, and mixture composition. Cold-region exposure is considered a demanding service-qualification case rather than as a separate material theme. Freeze–thaw, salt exposure, and chloride transport are used to assess whether changes in pore-water distribution, air-void stability, interfaces, and crack connectivity remain beneficial under severe service conditions. The review concludes with a staged route from constituent characterization and mixture screening to mechanism verification, exposure-relevant testing, and field validation.

papers.title: Robustness-aware multi-objective optimization of injection molding processing conditions and cooling channel geometry
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract The optimization of injection molding is strongly affected by variations in operating conditions, which influence part quality, cycle time, and energy consumption. Traditional approaches focus on nominal conditions and neglect unavoidable process fluctuations, whereas robust optimization seeks solutions that remain stable under variability. However, robustness is usually imposed through a single predefined formulation, even though different formulations may yield different optimization outcomes. This work investigates how the choice of robustness formulation affects multi-objective optimization in injection molding, using a two-ring case study modeled in Moldex3D with artificial neural network surrogates and a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm. In a first stage, the operating conditions (melt and mold temperatures) are optimized by comparing variance-based, average, worst-case, and expectation-based formulations through their Pareto fronts and solution rankings. In a second stage, the analysis is extended to conformal cooling channel geometries (two-ring, three-ring, spiral, and zig-zag), assessing how robustness against operating-condition variability influences geometry selection. The formulation reshapes the Pareto fronts and the solution rankings at both levels, but changes the selected solution unevenly: the recommended operating point stays essentially fixed at the lower boundary of the operating window, whereas the preferred cooling-channel geometry and the cost of imposing robustness depend on the formulation, because near-equivalent designs differ widely in geometry. Robustness is therefore not a neutral metric and must be defined according to the application and to the level, process parameters, or cooling-channel design, at which the engineering decision is made. The reported insensitivity of the recommended operating point to the robustness formulation is specific to the present material (PP, Borealis Borcom BG055AI) and operating window, whereas the general result is the asymmetry between the process-parameter and geometry levels.

papers.title: Rooftop Photovoltaic Panel Segmentation in UAV Imagery Using Attention U-Net with a ResNet34 Encoder
papers.journal: Gümüşhane Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Enstitüsü Dergisi
papers.abstract: Today, satellite image analysis and mapping systems play a significant role in urban planning, energy management, potential assessment, and sustainable development studies. In addition to the difficulty and high cost of fieldwork, the analysis of observations delays potential assessment and detection efforts. To overcome this delay and high cost, the use of satellite imagery is among the most important methods that facilitate these processes. In this study, a deep learning-based method is proposed to detect solar power plants from satellite imagery. This proposed method combines the U-Net architecture with an attention mechanism with the pre-trained ResNet34 encoder, enabling the efficient integration of both low-level and high-level features. The Albumentations library was used for data augmentation during the model training process, and the images were resized to 256x256. In the post-processing stage, the Dense Conditional Random Fields (CRF) method was applied to improve the accuracy of the segmentation masks generated by the model. For the test subset of the PV01 dataset, 95% IoU, 97% Dice, 99% Precision, 97% Recall, and 98% Accuracy were achieved. These results lead to lower costs and sharper results in determining energy potential.

papers.title: Engineering Interface and Orientation to Construct BNNS/LM Heterostructures with High Thermal Conductivity and Electrical Insulation for Improved Phonon Transport
papers.abstract: Abstract The synergistic optimization of high thermal conductivity and electrical insulation is a key challenge in thermal interface materials (TIMs). Conventional ceramic-based composites are inherently incapable of reconciling the contradictory demands of thermal conduction, electrical insulation, and low brittleness, while liquid metal fillers are plagued by poor interfacial compatibility and the risk of leakage. To address these issues, a synergistic strategy integrating molecular interfacial modification and microstructural alignment is developed to construct boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS)/liquid metal (LM) heterostructures. Using H2O2-assisted chlorosulfonic acid intercalation, h-BN is efficiently exfoliated and hydroxylated. Thiomalic acid (TMA) serves as a bridge, achieving uniform LM anchoring on BNNS and preventing LM leakage at a high loading of 42 wt %. A pressure-induced orientation is further applied to vertically align BNNS/LM hybrids, generating preferentially oriented and interconnected thermally conductive networks. The resulting composite exhibits an out-of-plane thermal conductivity of 17.76 W m–1 K–1, while maintaining good electrical insulation with an electrical resistivity exceeding 6 × 109 Ω m. LED tests show that this material reduces LED chip temperature by 16.7 °C compared to a commercial thermal pad. This cross-scale synergistic strategy provides a material design solution that combines high thermal conductivity and electrical safety for thermal management of high-power-density electronic devices.

papers.title: Fast structural remodeling of Jatropha curcas thylakoids upon recovery underpins chloroplast resilience to drought
papers.abstract: Abstract Jatropha curcas is a moderate stem-succulent oil crop renowned for its drought tolerance. While the photosynthetic activity of drought-stressed and rewatered Jatropha curcas has been investigated, little is known about the effects of drought and rewatering on chloroplast integrity and thylakoid architecture, critical determinants of photosynthetic performance under stress. Here, we exposed J. curcas seedlings to 19 days of water withdrawal followed by rewatering. Leaf relative water content remained unchanged throughout, indicating efficient water retention. Leaf anatomy was largely preserved, but chloroplasts became slightly smaller. Small-angle neutron scattering and transmission electron microscopy revealed a 2–4 nm decrease in granum repeat distance under drought. Electron microscopy further showed that this decrease was stronger in palisade than in spongy parenchyma chloroplasts. In thylakoids, the photosynthetic complexes were adjusted differently under drought: photosystem (PS) I and light harvesting complex (LHC) II remained unchanged, whereas PSII complexes decreased, increasing the PSI/PSII and LHCII/PSII ratios. Among the remaining PSII, larger supercomplexes were proportionally enriched, suggesting their higher drought stability. These changes coincided with a moderate decrease in PSII activity ( F v /F m ) and increased non-photochemical quenching. After rewatering, granum repeat distances recovered within hours (0.5–1 h in spongy and 5 h in palisade chloroplasts), revealing the involvement of rapidly reversible membrane remodeling under drought, while full recovery of photosynthetic performance and thylakoid protein composition was slower, requiring days. The high plasticity and rapid recovery of the thylakoid architecture is proposed to enable Jatropha curcas to restore its drought-affected photosynthetic apparatus and resume photosynthesis once water becomes available.

papers.title: Binary systems based on fatty acids and alcohols as bio-based thermochromic phase change materials for thermal energy storage
papers.journal: Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetry
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, bio-based thermochromic phase change materials (TPCMs) were obtained for potential energy storage applications. The phenomenon of thermochromism enables the observation of color changes in TPCMs during phase transitions. Three-component thermochromic systems were prepared using bromocresol purple as the organic dye, stearic acid as the color developer, and behenyl alcohol as the organic solvent. Simultaneously, both fatty acid and alcohol acted as phase change materials. Different mass ratios of the components were prepared and analyzed. The resulting TPCM mixtures were examined by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, differential scanning calorimetry, and thermal imaging. The obtained TPCMs exhibited high melting enthalpy (ca. 150–200 J g −1 ) in the temperature range of 50–70 °C, good thermal stability up to approximately 190 °C (T3% ≈ 190 °C), and a pronounced thermochromic response (Δ E ≈ 30). These materials show potential for application not only as phase change energy storage media, but also as colorimetric indicators.

Three-component thermochromic systems were prepared using bromocresol purple as the organic dye, stearic acid as the color developer, and behenyl alcohol as the organic solvent. These materials show potential for application not only as phase change energy storage media, but also as colorimetric indicators.

papers.title: POSSIBILITIES OF SYNCHRONOUS THERMAL ANALYSIS FOR ASSESSING THE FIRE HAZARD PROPERTIES OF POLYMER MATERIALS
papers.journal: Problems of risk management in the technosphere
papers.abstract: The article discusses the possibilities of the synchronous thermal analysis method combined with infrared spectroscopy to assess the fire-hazardous properties of polymer materials using the example of two polyvinyl chloride materials, which are quartz-vinyl tiles and canvas for a stretch ceiling. The study was carried out on a synchronous thermal analyzer NETZSCH STA 449 F3 Jupiter at a heating rate of 20 °C/min to 900 °C in an atmospheric atmosphere with simultaneous analysis of volatile products using an IR Fourier spectrometer FSM-1201. It has been established that due to the content of an additional organic filler (wood flour), quartz vinyl decomposes in four stages, with the first stage (≈287 °C) characterized by an exothermic peak on the DSC curve, accompanied by intense release of HCl, CO and Co₂, which indicates possible flaming. The stretch ceiling fabric (plasticized PVC without combustible fillers) decomposes according to the scheme typical for PVC plastics in three stages; Up to temperatures above 405 °C, the active release of gaseous products is accompanied by the presence of exothermic peaks on the DSC curve, which indicates the absence of flaming . It is shown that the dynamics of the release of gaseous carbonyl compounds, HCl, CO, and co₂, determined by the characteristic bands in the IR spectra, allows us to identify temperature and time intervals in which the occurrence of flame combustion of the materials under consideration is possible. It is concluded that the STA–X method provides objective information on the thermal and oxidative degradation of polymers, thermal effects, and kinetics of gas release and can be used to assess the fire hazard of materials and predict their behavior in a fire.

papers.title: Polylactide‐polydimethylsiloxane copolymers enabled by one‐pot chain‐shuttling ring‐opening copolymerization: Synthesis, properties and chemical recycling
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of degradable and incompatible copolymers with tunable material properties has garnered significant attention. Direct copolymerization of lactide (LA) and hexamethylcyclotrisiloxane (D 3 ) faces severe technical barriers due to their significant structural and reactivity differences. In this study, one‐pot chain shuttling ring‐opening polymerization process for the copolymerization of LA and D 3 is reported using the Zn‐Co double metal cyanide as heterogeneous catalyst and propylene oxide (PO) as bridging intermediate. Copolymerization kinetic study shows that the polymerization of LA is dominant in the early stage, and the average molecular weight of the copolymer unimodally increases with monomer conversion. Mechanistic investigations based on experimental and computational studies support a dual‐cycle chain‐shuttling pathway, in which PO acts as an intermediate in the chain shuttling process between the LA‐PO and D 3 ‐PO copolymerization cycles. The as‐prepared copolymers with different chemical compositions exhibit tunable thermal properties. Moreover, the resulting copolymers can be depolymerized to regenerate LA and silicone oil, demonstrating their potential for chemical recyclability. This study presents a practical and versatile approach for the synthesis of degradable and incompatible copolymers.

papers.title: SOLID SOLUTION REGIONS AND PHASE EQUILIBRIA IN THE Ag8GeS6‒Ag7SiS5I SYSTEM
papers.journal: Scientific Bulletin of the Uzhhorod University Series «Chemistry»
papers.abstract: In this work, a physicochemical study of phase equilibria in the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system was carried out for the first time, which is of key importance for the development of new functional materials and solid electrolytes with enhanced ionic conductivity for all-solid-state power sources and energy storage systems. The relevance of the study is driven by the necessity to search for superionic conductors based on Ag+ silver cations that crystallize in the argyrodite structural type and combine high ionic mobility, chemical stability, and operational safety. Synthesized polycrystalline samples of the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system were investigated by differential thermal analysis (DTA) and X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) with indexing of diffraction patterns using the EXPO 2014 software. Based on experimental data, the complete phase diagram of the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system was constructed for the first time. It was established that a continuous series of solid solutions (Roozeboom Type I) is formed in the high-temperature region above the phase transition temperatures of the initial components. The smooth course of the liquidus and solidus curves confirms the complete mutual solubility of the components in the liquid and high-temperature solid states. Upon cooling, a solubility gap is observed, accompanied by the formation of a two-phase region coexisting terminal Ag8-xGe1-xSixS6-xIx solid solutions with the orthorhombic structure of LT-Ag8GeS6 (SG Pna21) and Ag8-xGe1-xSixS6-xIx solid solutions with a cubic structure based on Ag7SiS5I (space group F-43m). The homogeneity ranges of the terminal solid solutions exceed 25 and 60 mol.%, respectively. The compositional dependence of the unit cell volumes of the alloys is in good agreement with the identified boundaries of the phase regions. The formation mechanism of substitution solid solutions with the composition Ag8-xGe1-xSixS6-xIx was described via defect reactions in Kröger–Vink notation. It was demonstrated that simultaneous isovalent (Ge+4↔Si+4) and heterovalent (S-2↔I-) two-ion substitution is accompanied by the formation of additional silver cation vacancies. The emergence of new cation vacancies creates favorable conditions for reducing the activation energy of Ag+ ion migration and serves as a prerequisite for increasing ionic conductivity. The asymmetry in the extent of the boundary solid solutions was explained within the polarity of isomorphism, taking into account the size factor and unit cell volume. It was shown that the cubic structure of Ag7SiS5I, featuring a larger cell volume and longer interatomic distances, significantly more effectively relaxes local structural stresses upon the incorporation of the Ge+4 ion, which accounts for its wider homogeneity range. The obtained results establish a fundamental framework for the targeted design of new solid electrolytes with controlled defect structure and high ionic conductivity.

Synthesized polycrystalline samples of the Ag8GeS6–Ag7SiS5I system were investigated by differential thermal analysis (DTA) and X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) with indexing of diffraction patterns using the EXPO 2014 software. The obtained results establish a fundamental framework for the targeted design of new solid electrolytes with controlled defect structure and high ionic conductivity.

papers.title: Preparation and application of functional hydroxyethyl cellulose hydrogels containing β-cyclodextrin complexes for cosmetic materials
papers.abstract: To address the formulation challenges associated with cosmetic active ingredients, including degradation, oxidation, and potential skin irritation, functional supramolecular inclusion complexes were prepared by a coprecipitation method using arbutin, niacinamide, and benzoic acid as guest molecules and β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) as the host. Unlike conventional single-component encapsulation approaches, this study proposes a novel multi-component co-delivery strategy for the simultaneous incorporation of multiple skin-brightening agents and a poorly water-soluble preservative into a single delivery platform. The potential host–guest interactions and complexation behavior were investigated using UV–Vis spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR) spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM). The resulting inclusion complexes were subsequently incorporated into a hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC)-based hydrogel to formulate multifunctional topical lotions. The formulations exhibited weakly acidic pH values of 5.53 and 5.55, within the range generally considered compatible with human skin. Rheological and texture profile analyses demonstrated pseudoplastic (shear-thinning) behavior and appropriate mechanical properties, including hardness, adhesiveness, and cohesiveness, for topical application. Furthermore, disk diffusion assays demonstrated antifungal activity against Candida albicans in the formulations containing the benzoic acid/β-CD inclusion complex. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the integration of multi-component β-CD inclusion complexes into an HEC hydrogel network yields functional formulations with potential as cosmetic platforms.

papers.title: Formulation and characterization of solid dispersion adsorbate of Candesartan Cilexetil: in vitro dissolution and in vivo performance
papers.abstract: Introduction Candesartan Cilexetil (CC) is a non-peptide angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonist widely used in the treatment of hypertension. However, CC has poor aqueous solubility (0.006 ± 0.002 mg/mL), low oral bioavailability (15%) and undergoes significant first-pass metabolism. Methods Candesartan Cilexetil Solid Dispersion adsorbate (CC-SDAs) was formulated by the fusion method, employing polyethylene glycol (PEG) 4000 as a hydrophilic carrier and Neusilin® US2 as an adsorbent, to improve the solubility, dissolution, and oral bioavailability of CC. The formulation was optimized using a 3 2 factorial design. Results and Discussion The optimized SDA formulation exhibited the following properties: Carr’s index (9.86 ± 0.09%), Hausner’s ratio (1.10 ± 0.16) and angle of repose (26.00 ± 0.19°), which shows improved flow property. DSC and XRD studies confirmed the conversion of the crystalline drug into an amorphous form. The optimized SDA formulation achieved %CDR of 90.41 ± 0.95% at Q30 min, demonstrating a marked improvement in in vitro dissolution compared to the pure drug (%CDR of 57.20 ± 3.78% at Q30 min). Furthermore, in vivo pharmacokinetic studies revealed a 2.02-fold enhanced oral bioavailability of CC from the SDA formulation compared to the CC suspension. Therefore, the SDA technique proves to be a promising approach for enhancing the solubility and dissolution of poorly water-soluble drugs.

papers.title: Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II: Changing health impacts of global ozone exposure
papers.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
papers.abstract: As part of the second Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report (TOAR-II), we synthesize global observations and observationally constrained estimates of surface-level ozone (O3) with contemporary literature to characterize the global distribution and trends of long-term O3 exposure, focusing on two health-relevant metrics and health impacts attributable to long-term exposure. The highest 2016-2020 surface-level O3 concentrations are observed or estimated in South Asia, eastern China, and parts of the Middle East and North Africa. From 2000 to 2020, O3 declined across southeastern North America and parts of Eastern Europe, while the largest increases occurred in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Global premature mortality from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) attributable to long-term O3 exposure nearly doubled between 2000 and 2020, reaching approximately 500 000 deaths annually. This overall increase obscures decreasing attributable deaths across North America and Europe and increasing deaths across large parts of the Global South. To spur high-quality, robust research on O3 health impacts, we summarize state-of-the-science practices for conducting health impact assessments (HIAs) and characterizing associated uncertainty. We also call for expanded in situ monitoring, improved health datasets and epidemiologic evidence, and sustained precursor emission reductions to clarify and limit the growing global health burden of O3 under climate change and demographic shifts. This article is part of the theme issue 'Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report II'.

papers.title: Gastrodia elata in neurological disorders: a systematic review of anti-inflammatory mechanisms and cross-disease therapeutic potential
papers.abstract: Background Neuroinflammation serves as a common pathological substrate across various neurological disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, and neuroimmune conditions. Key pathogenic mechanisms underlying these disorders include aberrant microglial activation, sustained release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and dysregulation of critical signaling cascades, particularly the NLRP3 inflammasome, NF-κB, and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways, all of which collectively contribute to progressive neuronal damage and functional decline. Objectives This review aims to systematically evaluate the preclinical evidence for the neuroprotective effects of Gastrodia elata Blume and its major bioactive constituents—gastrodin, parishin, p-hydroxybenzyl alcohol, and G. elata polysaccharides—in the treatment of Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease, acute ischemic stroke, vascular dementia, and epilepsy, with a particular focus on their modulation of inflammation-related signaling pathways. Methods A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang databases from inception to May 2026. Original studies investigating G. elata or its components in animal or cellular models of the aforementioned diseases and reporting inflammatory mechanisms were included. Results G. elata and its active constituents regulate multiple neuroinflammation-associated signaling pathways, including Nrf2/HO-1, NF-κB/NLRP3, JAK2/STAT3, and MAPK, thereby suppressing inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, these effects are primarily manifested as: (1) inhibition of microglial M1 polarization and consequent reduction of pro-inflammatory cytokine release; (2) blockade of inflammation-induced neuronal death through suppression of ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and apoptosis; (3) enhancement of Nrf2 nuclear translocation, leading to upregulation of antioxidant enzymes and attenuation of oxidative stress-mediated inflammation (e.g., ROS-driven cascades); and (4) modulation of the gut microbiota–brain axis to reduce both peripheral and central low-grade chronic inflammation. Conclusion Despite certain limitations in the existing evidence, this review clearly identifies future research priorities, including investigation of non-gastrodin active components, causal validation using gene-knockout models, and development of brain-targeted delivery strategies. These findings provide a valuable reference for the mechanism-guided development of neuroprotective agents derived from G. elata .

papers.title: Antibody-drug conjugates therapy for triple-negative breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Purpose This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) vs. conventional chemotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and to provide evidence for clinical decision-making and guideline development. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library and extracted data including hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), odds ratio (OR) for safety, and objective response rate (ORR). Results This study ultimately included 6 articles (5 dedicated RCTs for TNBC and 1 exploratory analysis of an HR-negative/HER2-low subgroup from the DESTINY-Breast04 trial), including 2,479 patients (1,256 patients in ADCs treatment and 1,223 patients in conventional chemotherapy). HR for PFS was 0.48 [95% CI (0.38, 0.61), P = 0.001], and HR for OS was 0.60 [95% CI (0.46, 0.79), P = 0.027]. OR for incidence of all adverse events (AEs) was 1.05 [95% CI (0.86,1.29), P = 0.901], and OR for incidence of grade ≥ 3 AEs was 1.11 [95% CI (0.88, 1.42), P = 0.984]. The pooled results demonstrated that ADCs significantly improved OS and PFS, while showing no significant increase in overall AEs or grade ≥ 3 AEs compared to control. Conclusion This study suggests that ADCs significantly improve OS and PFS without significantly increasing grade ≥ 3 AEs compared to conventional chemotherapy in TNBC, providing support for clinical decision-making and guideline development. These findings may inform future head-to-head trials, optimization of ADC-based combination regimens, and biomarker-guided precision treatment. As clinical data on novel ADCs continue to accumulate, these conclusions may be further validated and extended.

papers.title: Structure–Function Relationships of a High-Molecular-Weight Exopolysaccharide from Euhalothece sp. with Bioactive and Emulsifying Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyanobacterial exopolysaccharides (EPSs) are promising sustainable biopolymers, yet halotolerant strains remain comparatively underexplored and the relationships between EPS composition and functionality are still not well-defined. In this study, an EPS produced by Euhalothece sp. AQUAMEB-3 was isolated and characterized to assess its physicochemical properties, compositional features, and multifunctional performance. The EPS was identified as a high-molecular-weight (Mw ∼ 2617 kDa), strongly anionic heteropolysaccharide with a zeta potential of −45.1 mV, composed mainly of xylose, fucose, amino sugars, and uronic acids. FTIR, 1H NMR, 1H–1H correlation spectroscopy (COSY) NMR, and GC–MS analyses indicated a structurally heterogeneous polymer, while XRD and SEM revealed a predominantly amorphous and porous morphology. The EPS also exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behavior and strong water affinity. Functionally, the EPS showed high emulsifying performance, with E24 values reaching 94.2% at 1.0% (w/v), comparable to xanthan gum under the tested conditions, and maintained emulsion stability over extended storage. It also displayed antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli (MIC: 150 μg mL–1) and Staphylococcus aureus (MIC: 300 μg mL–1), together mL–1 with concentration-dependent antioxidant and iron-chelating activities, reaching 82.6% radical scavenging and 96% metal chelation at the highest tested concentrations. Cytotoxicity assays indicated concentration- and cell-type-dependent cytocompatibility. Taken together, these results define a distinct physicochemical and functional profile for the EPS produced by Euhalothece sp. AQUAMEB-3 and expand the available characterization data for halotolerant cyanobacterial exopolysaccharides. The observed associations between its compositional and physicochemical characteristics and functional properties should be regarded as correlative rather than mechanistically established. These findings support the potential of AQUAMEB-3 EPS for further investigation in emulsion stabilization and other biobased formulation applications.

papers.title: Macromolecular Fingerprints and Thermodynamic–Kinetic Regulation of Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation in Polysaccharide-Derived Biocondensates
papers.abstract: Abstract The relationship between chemical functionalization and the thermoresponsive phase separation of polysaccharide-derived biocondensates remains insufficiently investigated. In this study, we systematically examine how the substitution site, polymer concentration, solvent environment, and thermal history influence the phase behavior of methacrylated dextran derivatives using multidimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, diffusion-ordered spectroscopy (DOSY), temperature-dependent turbidimetry, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), and live time-lapse microscopy. NMR analysis revealed preferential methacrylation of C2 and C3 hydroxyl positions at low degrees of substitution, with increasing functionalization at the C4 position as the substitution degree increases. DOSY measurements further demonstrated distinct solvent- and substitution-dependent changes in polymer mobility under aqueous-phase-separating conditions. The lower critical solution temperature decreased as the Dex-MA concentration increased and shifted to higher temperatures with an increasing heating rate. Repeated thermal cycling progressively altered the transition temperature and reduced thermal hysteresis, particularly at higher concentrations, demonstrating a pronounced thermal-history dependence. ITC characterizations showed concentration- and temperature-dependent exothermic responses associated with polymer–solution interactions, while live imaging directly captured the progressive nucleation, growth, and coalescence of polymer-rich domains upon heating. Together, these findings establish molecular-to-mesoscale relationships linking chemical functionalization, polymer–solvent interactions, and thermodynamic–kinetic factors to the liquid–liquid phase separation of methacrylated polysaccharides, providing insights for the rational design of thermoresponsive polysaccharide-based biomaterials.

papers.title: Resveratrol‐Loaded Fe‐Pt@UiO‐66‐NH 2 Nanoformulation With pH‐Triggered Release and ROS Generation for Synergistic Anticancer and Antibacterial Therapy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Preventing wound infections and postoperative tumor recurrence remains challenging due to bacterial infection risks and potential cancer cell metastasis. The formulation was prepared by incorporating Fe‐Pt NPs via a solvothermal method, followed by resveratrol (RES) loading. Antibacterial assays show that the formulation damages the surface morphology of E. coli and S. aureus by enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, leading to potent sterilization. Consequently, the pH‐responsive RES@Fe‐Pt@MOF nanoformulation demonstrates superior antimicrobial and anticancer activities under mildly acidic conditions, highlighting its potential for postoperative cancer therapy.

papers.title: Metal–Organic Framework Synthesis Strategies for Efficient Encapsulation and Sustained Release of Bioactive Compounds
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as versatile carriers for biomedical applications because of their tunable porosity, high surface area, and structural robustness. Their biocompatibility depends on carefully selecting nontoxic metals such as Fe, Zn, or Mg; safe organic ligands, including carboxylates, imidazolates, and pyridines; and stabilizing coatings such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), chitosan, and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) that enhance aqueous stability and enable controlled release. Conventional synthesis methods typically yield highly crystalline frameworks but require long reaction times and extensive solvent use. In contrast, nonconventional approaches are gaining popularity for their faster, energy-efficient methods. Techniques such as microwave irradiation, sonochemical activation, and electrochemical synthesis provide rapid, controllable conditions that reduce energy consumption and shorten reaction times. In particular, mechanochemical encapsulation is an eco-friendly, sustainable, scalable, and high-yield methodology that enables in situ entrapment of bioactive molecules and enhances adsorption capacity. Moreover, the mechanochemical methodology enables modulation of physicochemical parameters such as morphology and particle size, which critically influence adsorption behavior and host-guest interactions. Examples of encapsulation processes involving antidiabetic agents, anticancer therapeutics, and antioxidants are presented, and these can be translated into mechanochemical approaches. In this regard, MOFs stand out as promising platforms for targeted delivery and sustained release. Integrating rational component selection, coating strategies, and sustainable synthesis methodologies positions MOFs as next-generation biocompatible carriers for precision biomedical applications.

Integrating rational component selection, coating strategies, and sustainable synthesis methodologies positions MOFs as next-generation biocompatible carriers for precision biomedical applications.

papers.title: Carbonation–hydration interplay in CO2-cured Portland cement: Mechanistic insights into early-stage strength development
papers.abstract: Carbonation curing has emerged as a promising strategy for simultaneous strength enhancement and CO 2 sequestration in cement-based materials. However, the fundamental interplay between carbonation and hydration, and its implications for strength development, remains insufficiently understood. Since the formation of CaCO 3 consumes reactive clinker phases, it is unclear whether carbonation promotes or hinders hydration during early-age curing. This study systematically investigates the carbonation–hydration interplay in CO 2 -cured OPC by controlling pre-curing durations (6–30 h) prior to CO 2 exposure. A combination of XRD-Rietveld analysis, FTIR, BSE imaging, and MIP was employed to quantify phase evolution, microstructure, and pore characteristics. Results show that moderate pre-curing (12–18 h) optimizes the balance between hydration and carbonation, leading to enhanced clinker reactivity, reduced total porosity, and significantly improved early compressive strength. In contrast, extended pre-curing (>24 h) or excessive carbonation reduces strength development due to calcium depletion, limited CO 2 diffusion, and pore coarsening. Microstructural and chemical analyses reveal a dual role of carbonation: it accelerates early hydration through Ca 2+ consumption and nucleation effects, while prolonged carbonation progressively suppresses hydration by forming dense carbonate products and altering pore connectivity. These findings demonstrate that carbonation and hydration exhibit both competitive and synergistic interactions, with their relative contributions governed by the timing of CO 2 exposure within the investigated pre-curing window. This work provides mechanistic insights into optimizing CO 2 -curing regimes for improved performance and carbon efficiency in cement-based materials.

papers.title: Impact of Type and Content of Nanocellulose on Phenol–Resorcinol–Formaldehyde Resin’s Cure Kinetics, Rheology, and Flexural Properties
papers.abstract: Phenol–resorcinol–formaldehyde (PRF) is a cold-setting wood adhesive whose cured form is intrinsically brittle and whose bonding effectiveness deteriorates with storage age due to the loss of reactive methylol groups. This study investigated the potential of nanocellulose (NC) reinforcement to enhance toughness and offset aging-related losses. Before the hardener was added, three NC types—cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) and bleached and unbleached cellulose nanofibers (BNF, UBNF)—were homogenized into fresh (NP) and 4-year-aged (OP) PRF resin at one and three weight percent. The resin was then cast and gradually post-cured. Differential scanning calorimetry and rheometry were used to track curing activity, and flexural characteristics were assessed on cured specimens. The inclusion of NC increased the temperature at which gelation began, prolonging the working time of the resin. In comparison to neat PRF, CNF (BNF/UBNF) integration enhanced flexural strength by up to 39%, while CNC addition increased flexural modulus by up to 57%. Fibril aggregation was responsible for the 12–20% decrease in BNF/UBNF strength at three weight percent loading. Aged PRF was regularly outperformed by fresh PRF composites. These findings support the use of NC reinforcement in wood–PRF composites for extrusion-based additive manufacturing by demonstrating that it can toughen PRF and restore characteristics lost due to resin aging.

papers.title: Biophysical Characterization of Interactions Between Human Salivary Proteins and Quinine
papers.abstract: Saliva is the first biological medium encountered by bitter compounds in the oral cavity, and salivary proteins have been indirectly implicated in bitterness perception. However, direct biophysical characterization of salivary protein-bitterant interactions has not been reported. This study investigated interactions between salivary proteins and the model bitterant quinine using complementary biophysical techniques. Pooled whole saliva (WS) from 44 healthy volunteers was separated into high- (HMW) and low-molecular-weight (LMW) fractions using a 3 kDa filter. Protein-quinine interactions were characterized by fluorescence spectroscopy, sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation (SV-AUC), and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Fluorescence spectroscopy showed a concentration-dependent reduction in the apparent unbound quinine, reaching 59.28 ± 0.89% at 0.6 mg/mL protein in WS, with greater apparent binding in the LMW fraction than the HMW fraction. SV-AUC provided evidence of protein-quinine complex formation, with the LMW fraction exhibiting the clearest changes through the appearance of new, higher sedimentation coefficient species, suggesting quinine-induced multimerization. ITC revealed endothermic binding across all three saliva systems, with the LMW fraction exhibiting the greatest change in apparent binding enthalpy (∆H = 1.053 ± 0.009 kcal/ mol) compared with WS (∆H = 0.321 ± 0.548 kcal/ mol) and HMW fraction (∆H = 0.081 ± 0.158 kcal/ mol). These findings converge to demonstrate that human salivary proteins interact with quinine, with the LMW species (< 3 kDa) exhibiting the strongest apparent binding (17.53 ± 1.58% reduction in unbound quinine at 0.2 mg/mL protein from the fluorescence measurements). This work provides the first biophysical characterization of salivary protein-bitterant interactions and establishes a foundation for future investigations into the role of salivary proteins in bitterness perception. papers.title: Adipose-derived stem cell extracellular vesicles in diabetic microangiopathy: from pathological networks to clinical translation
papers.abstract: Diabetic microangiopathy (DMA) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in diabetes. Its pathogenesis involves interconnected processes, including metabolic disturbance, oxidative stress, inflammation, immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial abnormalities, and impaired tissue repair. This complexity suggests that therapeutic strategies targeting individual pathways may be insufficient to address the multidimensional pathological processes underlying DMA. Adipose-derived stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (ADSC-EVs) have emerged as potential cell-free therapeutic candidates whose multimolecular cargo may modulate multiple disease-relevant processes. Preclinical evidence suggests that ADSC-EVs can influence oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, immune responses, and tissue repair, providing a potential basis for multitarget modulation of pathological microenvironments. This review critically evaluates organ-specific evidence for ADSC-EVs in diabetic retinopathy, diabetic kidney disease, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and diabetic chronic wounds, with particular attention to evidence specificity, therapeutic mechanisms, delivery barriers, and translational limitations. We further summarize advances in EV engineering, including parent-cell and cargo engineering, surface modification, biomaterial integration, and stimuli-responsive delivery, while distinguishing ADSC-EV-specific findings from evidence extrapolated from the broader EV field. Finally, we discuss major barriers to clinical translation, including manufacturing standardization, potency assessment, biodistribution, organ-specific delivery, long-term safety, and regulatory evaluation. Future studies integrating disease stratification, multi-omics, rational engineering, and standardized manufacturing may help determine whether the multitarget effects of ADSC-EVs can be translated into reproducible and clinically meaningful therapies for DMA.

papers.title: Pediatric-friendly Smart Oro-solid Carbamazepine Dry Suspension (SOS-CDS): optimization, functionality and in-vivo taste determination
papers.journal: Bulletin of the National Research Centre/Bulletin of the National Research Center
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Pediatric formulations are challenging to design due to considerations of convenience. Many children are suffering from an epileptic condition at an early age. Continuing anti-epileptic treatment can influence bone metabolism in children. The research was undertaken to design a pediatric and industry approachable smart stable dosage form of carbamazepine (CBZ) supplemented with Vitamin D (Vit D). Methods Smart Oro-solid Carbamazepine Dry Suspension (SOS-CDS) was formulated using a liquorice-based suspending agent. DSC and FTIR were performed to observe interactions among CBZ, Vit D, and other excipients. Screening of various variables was performed using Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and the results were further optimized using a Central Composite Design (CCD) with two independent variables (suspending agent and mixing speed) and three dependent variables (sedimentation volume, blend uniformity, and %CDR). The designed SOS-CDS was evaluated for its stability and other physicochemical parameters. BATA model was utilized to assess the taste masking of carbamazepine. Results DSC and FTIR spectra showed no interaction between the drug and excipients. QbD approach successfully optimized the SOS-CDS, identifying suspending agent concentration and mixing speed as critical variables. A total of 13 experiments were designed and evaluated. Optimized SOS-CDS showed good micromeritics properties and a desired sedimentation volume, with 93.7% release at 420 min. BATA model revealed the taste masking of CBZ. Conclusion The major concern with the current formulation was its instability in the presence of light and moisture. The developed SOS-CDS was stable due to its intelligent mechanism. In addition, long-term use of CBZ causes bone degeneration, which may be overcome by supplementing Vitamin D. Liquorice was explored as a masking agent for the bitter taste of CBZ and was confirmed in the BATA model. The newer SOS-CDS was stable and had controlled release. The developed formulation will be useful at an industrial scale.

papers.title: Disentangled Ultrahigh-Molecular-Weight Polyethylene by Boroxide Complexes of Half-Titanocenes via Hydrogen Bonding Interaction
papers.abstract: Abstract The disentangled state of ultrahigh-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) is of practical importance to its processability, but the direct synthesis of disentangled UHMWPE (dis-UHMWPE) remains highly challenging. Herein, a series of half-titanocenes Cp′Ti(L)Cl2 (Cp′ = cyclopentadienyl derivatives; L = (Ar2)BO–) bearing electron-withdrawing boroxide ancillary ligands have been developed for ethylene polymerization. Although the steric and electronic modifications of Cp′ and boroxide ancillary ligands impact catalytic activity, the substituted boroxide-containing half-titanocenes produce UHMWPE with viscosity-average molecular weights (Mv) of >1 × 106 g/mol under regular polymerization conditions. The resultant UHMWPEs feature a low degree of chain entanglement as confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) annealing studies and melt rheological tests. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal that the formation of dis-UHMWPE originates from the hydrogen bonding interaction between the electron-withdrawing boroxide ancillary ligand and β-H on the growing polymer chain, which promotes chain growth and suppresses β-H elimination chain transfer.

papers.title: Rice starch–activated carbon composite films for potential cosmetic facial sheet mask applications: physicochemical and mechanical characterization
papers.abstract: Abstract The widespread use of synthetic facial sheet masks has raised concerns about their environmental impact. In this study, rice starch (RS)–activated carbon (AC) composite films were prepared by solution casting and characterized to assess their potential as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. The surface morphology of the films changed after AC incorporation, with thicknesses ranging from approximately 0.2 to 0.3 mm and the moisture content increasing with increasing AC loading. The water contact angles ranged from 48.95° to 63.85°, indicating hydrophilic surfaces, with the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibiting the lowest measured contact angle. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested predominantly physical interactions between the RS and AC, whereas differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction characterized their thermal transitions and structural features. Compared with the neat RS film, the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibited lower tensile strength and elongation at break. MTT assays performed on AC powder revealed that the cell viability of L929 fibroblasts and HaCaT keratinocytes was above 90% under the tested conditions; the complete composite films were not evaluated for cytotoxicity. Soil burial testing revealed approximately 68.7% mass loss for the RS + AC film after 30 days. These findings support further investigations of RS + AC films as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. Their biocompatibility, water uptake, serum retention, and performance during skin application remain to be established.

papers.title: Equol–Thiophene‐Based Benzoxazine: Synthesis, Curing Kinetics, and Blend Properties
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A novel biobased bifunctional benzoxazine monomer EQ‐tma was successfully synthesized via Mannich condensation using equol and 2‐thiophenemethylamine as starting materials. The chemical structure of the monomer was confirmed by 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, FT‐IR, and high‐resolution mass spectrometry. The curing kinetics of EQ‐tma were investigated by non‐isothermal DSC, and the apparent activation energies determined by the Kissinger, Ozawa, and Starink methods were 93.94, 97.21, and 87.50 kJ/mol, respectively, indicating that the curing reaction followed an autocatalytic model, and the kinetic equation was accordingly established. EQ‐tma was then blended with commercial PH‐ddm, and the curing mechanism of the blends was studied by in situ FT‐IR. TGA analysis demonstrated that the incorporation of EQ‐tma improved the thermal stability of the commercial benzoxazine, while DMA was employed to evaluate the thermomechanical properties of the resultant co‐polymers. This study provides new insights into the molecular design of biobased benzoxazines and reveals their formulation potential when blended with benzoxazine commercial system.

papers.title: RECENT ADVANCES IN MUCOADHESIVE MICROSPHERES FOR ORAL CONTROLLED DRUG DELIVERY: FORMULATION STRATEGIES, CHARACTERIZATION, THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Mucoadhesive microspheres have emerged as one of the most promising oral controlled drug delivery systems due to their ability to prolong gastrointestinal residence time, improve drug bioavailability, and enhance patient compliance. These multiparticulate systems adhere to the mucosal surface, thereby extending drug absorption and minimizing dosing frequency. Various natural and synthetic polymers, including Carbopol, Chitosan, Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose (HPMC), Sodium Alginate, and Eudragit polymers, have been extensively investigated for the preparation of mucoadhesive microspheres. Different preparation techniques such as solvent evaporation, ionotropic gelation, spray drying, and emulsion cross-linking have been successfully employed to formulate microspheres with desirable physicochemical characteristics. The performance of these systems is evaluated through particle size analysis, drug entrapment efficiency, swelling behavior, mucoadhesive strength, zeta potential, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and in-vitro drug release studies. Mucoadhesive microspheres have been successfully used for antihypertensive, anti-diabetic, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer medications, according to recent studies. Research on mucoadhesive microspheres loaded with nifedipine has demonstrated longer therapeutic efficacy, better entrapment efficiency, and sustained drug release, suggesting their potential for controlled oral drug administration. There are still issues with large-scale production, reproducibility, regulatory approval, and long-term stability despite tremendous advancements. Future studies should concentrate on Quality by Design (QbD), artificial intelligence-based formulation optimization, smart polymers, and mucoadhesive systems aided by nanotechnology.

papers.title: Effects of nitrogen rates and pulsed versus continuous subsurface drip irrigation on gas exchange in sugarcane
papers.abstract: Abstract The pulse irrigation presents itself as a strategy capable of contributing to the efficient management of water and nitrogen, resulting in the optimization of agricultural cultivation. The objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of the application of nitrogen doses, applied via pulse and continuous fertigation, on gas exchange in sugarcane crops. For this, a field experiment was set up at the Carpina Sugarcane Experimental Station (EECAC) in the State of Pernambuco, Brazil. The experimental design was randomized blocks, in a 5 × 2 factorial scheme, with five nitrogen doses (80, 120, 160, 240 and 320 kg ha − 1 ) and two types of irrigation application (pulse and continuous), with four replicates. At 240 and 300 DAH, gas exchange evaluations were performed. Pulse irrigation combined with an estimated N dose of 189.4 kg ha − 1 , determined through regression analysis, promoted higher net photosynthesis in sugarcane. Applying nitrogen doses higher than 168.4 kg ha − 1 reduced carboxylation efficiency and water use, indicating a physiological limit for the nutrient. Pulse irrigation improved net photosynthesis, transpiration, stomatal conductance, internal CO 2 concentration, instantaneous water use efficiency, intrinsic water use efficiency and instantaneous carboxylation efficiency, highlighting the potential of integrated management of irrigation and nitrogen fertilization in the physiological performance of the crop.

papers.title: The future of salicylic acid in agriculture lies in precision priming
papers.abstract: As the world is moving towards enforcing strict regulations against pesticides, plant hormones triggering natural defenses represent a foundation of sustainable agriculture. Among them, Salicylic acid (SA) is a major phytohormone for governing systemic acquired resistance (SAR), a broad-spectrum immune response, against hemibiotrophic and biotrophic pathogens. Although it has huge potential as a sustainable alternative to synthetic pesticides, its field efficacy lags, with inconsistent disease control, phytotoxicity, and significant yield loss. This review gathers emerging evidence to explain the inconsistency of SA-mediated disease control under field conditions and proposes priming-based frameworks to improve reliability in crop protection systems. It focuses on two underexplored areas. First, the metabolic and hormonal basis of the growth-defense trade-off. Second, the climate-induced signaling failure, where elevated temperatures disrupt the SA transcriptional machinery. Simultaneously, the review explores emerging innovative strategies, such as nano-formulations for controlled release, synthetic analogues with enhanced stability, and the paradigm shift from direct induction to molecular priming to solve the existing problems. By integrating findings from the model and crop species, we infer that the future of SA in agriculture does not lie in direct, high-dose application in the field. Instead, it lies in the development of intelligent, climate-resilient priming systems that work in alignment with plant biology.

papers.title: Integrated microbiome and metabolomic analysis reveals associations between vaginal microbiota composition and psychological profiles
papers.abstract: The vaginal microbiota plays a key role in women’s health and is increasingly linked to psychobiological processes, although underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between vaginal community state types (CSTs), psychological dimensions, and vaginal metabolites in 105 reproductive-aged women. Vaginal microbiota composition was characterised through 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and classified into CSTs; metabolomic profiling was performed using NMR spectroscopy. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing trait anxiety, emotion regulation, behavioural inhibition/activation, depressive symptoms, perceived stress, and somatisation. Women with polymicrobial CST IV profiles showed significantly lower Behavioural Activation System (BAS)-Reward Responsiveness and BAS-Drive scores, whereas those with Lactobacillus iners -dominated CST III exhibited lower Behavioural Inhibition System (BIS) scores. Limited direct correlations between bacterial taxa and psychological variables emerged, but psychological dimensions strongly correlated with specific vaginal metabolites. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated that aminobutyrate and valine partially or fully mediated the associations between CST IV and BAS dimensions, while phenylalanine partially mediated the relationship between CST IV and BIS inhibition. These findings suggest that the vaginal metabolome may represent a functional interface linking microbial community structure and psychological functioning, supporting a biopsychosocial perspective of vaginal health and the importance of integrating microbiome, metabolomic, and psychological assessments in women’s health research.

papers.title: Atom‐Efficient Cerium‐Based Molecular Cages as Biocompatible Reactive Oxygen Scavengers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐scavenging materials for biomedical applications has been constrained by the difficulty associated with achieving simultaneously broad‐spectrum scavenging efficiency and acceptable biosafety. To date, ceria/nanoceria systems have been explored for this purpose; however, they suffer from limited cerium‐atom utilization. Inspired by the atom‐economy concept of single‐atom catalysis, we report a cerium‐based molecular‐cage strategy for treating oxidative stress‐driven atherosclerosis (AS). It involves mixed‐valent cerium ions (Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ ) that are stably confined within tailored molecular cages and that mimic the cooperation between oxygen vacancies and cerium redox cycling in CeO 2 . This endows the four representative cages of this study with an ability to scavenge superoxide anion (O 2 • − ), hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), and hydroxyl radical (•OH). Their catalytic function can be readily modulated through the ROS‐responsive release of the molecular cages at local lesion sites. This capability was found to alleviate oxidative stress and associated inflammation, as inferred from the finding that a lead cerium cage incorporated into a biocompatible nanoparticle reduces the progression of AS in a mouse model. A reduction in plaque lipid deposition, macrophage accumulation, necrotic core formation, and MMP‐9‐associated matrix was seen.

papers.title: PLA/BioAlSr composite films for tendon–bone interface regeneration: effect of bioactive glass content on morphology, mechanical behavior, degradation and bioactivity
papers.journal: Journal of Applied Materials and Technology
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in implant materials engineering is combining mechanical strength, moldability, biocompatibility, bioresorbability, and osteoactivity within a single material. This work develops poly(lactic acid) (PLA) films loaded with a strontium- and alumina-containing bioactive glass (BioAlSr), explored as a candidate material for metallic-implant coatings and, prospectively, tendon–bone interface grafts. Melt-quenched glass powder (mean diameter 5 µm) was incorporated at 15, 30, 50 and 70 wt% by solvent casting. Characterization covered microscopy with TGA, EDS, XRD, tensile testing, swelling in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) with pH monitoring, cytotoxicity and bioactivity in simulated body fluid (SBF). Particles were mechanically embedded, with no evidence of strong interfacial bonding. Tensile strength peaked at 15 wt% (15 ± 1 MPa) and fell sharply already by 30 wt% (6.1 ± 1.3 MPa), continuing to decline at 50–70 wt% (3 ± 2 to 2.5 ± 6 MPa); elongation at break fell from 61 ± 17 % for neat PLA to 13 % at 15–30 wt% and below 5 % at 50–70 wt%, while Young's modulus (63–72 MPa) was comparatively insensitive to glass content. After 28 days in PBS, swelling ranged from 2.1 % (30 wt%) to 8.6 % (70 wt%) against 2.7 % for neat PLA, and pH rose from 7.2 to 9.0–10.6 for loadings ? 30 wt%, remaining near 7.3 for neat PLA and 15 wt%. In neutral red uptake, undiluted extract gave 89 % viability for 15 wt% and 66 % for 30 wt%, against 46 % for neat PLA (NCTC clone 929); the 50 and 70 wt% films reduced viability to 63 % at 100 mg mL?¹ (NIH/3T3). No composite reached IC50, and all were less cytotoxic than neat PLA. After SBF immersion, all glass-loaded films developed a crystalline calcium-phosphate phase while EDS confirmed progressive Ca and P surface enrichment, supporting apatite-like mineralization. Glass content therefore trades mechanical performance against degradation and bioactivity; 15–30 wt% was retained as the working range for its favorable combination of tensile strength and particle-dispersion homogeneity relative to 50–70 wt%, notwithstanding PVBio30's cytotoxicity falling marginally below the ISO 10993-5 threshold.

papers.title: Seed balls with bauxite mining technosol: an alternative forest restoration technique in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
papers.abstract: Abstract This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of technosol, composed of clay cake and organic compost, as a substrate for seed balls using native species from the Atlantic Forest. We investigated how different substrate compositions and the addition of NPK fertilizer influence the emergence, survival, and growth of four native tree species: Senna macranthera , Enterolobium contortisiliquum , Pterogyne nitens , and Anadenanthera peregrina . Seedling emergence and survival were monitored continuously over 190 days, and growth performance was evaluated using logistic growth models. The results showed that, in terms of emergence and survival, treatments without NPK addition yielded the best outcomes, regardless of the proportion of clay cake and organic compost. Growth models revealed that non-pioneer species ( P. nitens and A. peregrina ) performed better under treatments without NPK, while pioneer species ( S. macranthera and E. contortisiliquum ) exhibited higher growth rates in treatments with NPK. These findings emphasize the importance of aligning substrate composition and fertilization with the ecological strategies of different species to optimize restoration outcomes. The use of technosol-based seed balls derived from bauxite mining represents a viable alternative for forest restoration, promoting biodiversity recovery, reducing waste disposal in tailings dams, and contributing to circular economy principles in the mining sector.
